```{r setup}
source("report_helpers.R")

d <- load_inputs(params$data_dir, params$repo)
aligned <- d$aligned
strains <- d$strains
reference <- d$reference

columns <- cen_columns(aligned)
boxes <- cde_boxes(columns)
variants <- call_variants(aligned, columns)
events <- variant_events(variants)
rates <- element_rates(events, aligned)
spectrum <- substitution_spectrum(variants, aligned, columns)

n_asm <- nrow(strains)
n_loci <- nrow(aligned)
n_cen <- n_distinct(aligned$centromere)
qc_tot <- colSums(d$qc[, -1])
n_cross <- qc_tot[["raw_hits"]] - qc_tot[["after_locus_assignment"]]
n_secondary <- if ("secondary_loci" %in% names(qc_tot)) qc_tot[["secondary_loci"]] else 0
n_merged <- qc_tot[["after_locus_assignment"]] - qc_tot[["final_loci"]] - n_secondary
n_cde_ok <- sum(aligned$cde_ok)
pct <- function(x) percent(x, accuracy = 1)
fmt <- function(x, d = 1) format(round(x, d), nsmall = d)

big <- aligned |> slice_max(delta_length, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
big_ins <- events |> filter(type == "Insertion") |> slice_max(size, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
rate_mean <- rates |> group_by(element, kind) |>
  summarise(per_kb = 1000 * sum(n) / sum(n_assemblies * element_length), .groups = "drop")
rate_of <- function(el, k) rate_mean$per_kb[rate_mean$element == el & rate_mean$kind == k]
n_indel_cdeii <- sum(events$type != "Substitution" & events$element == "CDEII")
n_indel <- sum(events$type != "Substitution")

# Shown on hover and in the figure files; a light/dark switch is not offered
assembly_rows <- length(levels(aligned$assembly))
# One row per assembly stops being readable (and exceeds the cairo surface limit of 32767 px)
# beyond a few dozen assemblies: large sets get a fixed-height static heatmap / per-column
# variant frequencies instead (LARGE_SET is also used in the chunk options below)
LARGE_SET <- 60
large_set <- assembly_rows > LARGE_SET
```

## From genomes to centromeres at a glance {#sec-workflow}

```{r fig-workflow}
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "How centromeres are mined from the assemblies and analysed. Counts are from this run; @sec-pipeline describes each step."
wf <- workflow_diagram(list(
  n_asm = n_asm, raw_hits = qc_tot[["raw_hits"]], n_cross = n_cross, n_merged = n_merged,
  n_loci = n_loci, n_cen = n_cen, n_cde_ok = n_cde_ok
))
```

## Scope and provenance {#sec-scope}

::: {.callout-important}
## Where these figures come from

Every figure and number below is **computed when this page is rendered**, from the
pipeline outputs in ``r params$data_dir``: **`r n_asm` telomere-to-telomere
assemblies** from the ScRAP collection ([O'Donnell et al. 2023](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-023-01459-y)),
**`r n_loci` centromere loci** (`r n_cen` per assembly). Re-render with
`quarto render report.qmd -P data_dir:<dir>` to rebuild it from a larger run.

With `r n_asm` assemblies this is a **development set**: it is enough to show what
each statistic looks like and whether the pipeline is right, not to make
population-level claims. Read every count as "in these `r n_asm` strains".
:::

### The biological object

*S. cerevisiae* has **point centromeres**: each of the 16 chromosomes carries a
short, genetically defined element of roughly **117–120 bp** (S288C annotation)
that is sufficient to build a kinetochore. This is unlike the megabase-scale
repeat arrays of most eukaryotes, and it is what makes a base-by-base comparison
across strains tractable at all. The element has three parts:

| Element | Size | Composition | Bound by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CDEI** | 8 bp | palindromic `RTCACRTG` | Cbf1 (non-essential, stabilising) |
| **CDEII** | ~78–86 bp | **>90 % A+T**, low complexity, length-variable | wraps the Cse4 (CENP-A) nucleosome |
| **CDEIII** | 26 bp | conserved, `CCGAA` core | CBF3 complex — **essential**; point mutations in the central CCG abolish function |

The expectation going in is asymmetric: **CDEI and CDEIII should be under strong
purifying selection** (protein-binding sites whose failure is lethal), while
**CDEII should tolerate** substitution and length change, because what it
contributes is a bendable AT-rich stretch of about the right length rather than a
specific sequence.

### What S288C is, and how it is used here

S288C is the standard laboratory strain and the first eukaryote ever sequenced
(1996); SGD's annotation of its 16 centromeres is the reference. It is used three
times: as the **BLAST query** that locates each centromere, as the source of the
**CDEI/CDEIII motif models**, and as the **row every strain is compared against**.
"Variant" in this report therefore means *difference from S288C*. It does not mean
*derived mutation*: S288C is one strain, and @sec-variants shows several places
where it is the one carrying the unusual allele.

## From genome to centromere table {#sec-pipeline}

```{r tbl-strains}
#| tbl-cap: "The assemblies. Strain metadata from Peter et al. 2018 (joined on the three-letter strain code). `_collapsed` = both haplotypes of a heterozygous genome merged into one sequence; `_1a`, `_3a` = one phased haplotype."
rearranged <- aligned |>
  filter(grepl("_", contig_name)) |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  summarise(rearranged = paste0(centromere, " on ", contig_name, collapse = "; "))
strains |>
  left_join(rearranged, by = "sample") |>
  transmute(Assembly = assembly, Accession = sample, Strain = strain, Clade = clade,
            Origin = paste(ecology, geography, sep = " · "), Ploidy = ploidy,
            Zygosity = zygosity,
            `CEN on a rearranged chromosome` = coalesce(rearranged, "")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**How the table was obtained.**

1. **Locate.** The 16 S288C centromeres are BLASTed (`blastn`, word size 7,
   e ≤ 1e-5) against each assembly.
2. **Assign each locus to one centromere.** CDEI and CDEIII are shared between
   centromeres, so a CEN15 query also hits the CEN14 locus weakly (and CEN10 ↔
   CEN11, CEN3 → CEN15). Overlapping hits form one locus, and the locus goes to
   the query with the best e-value.
3. **Merge split hits.** Pieces of one centromere that BLAST reported separately are
   joined.
4. **Annotate CDEs from the genome itself.** BLAST only says *where*. The locus ±150
   bp is cut from the assembly and oriented like S288C; CDEI and CDEIII are placed
   with position weight matrices built from the 16 S288C elements (CDEI = first 8
   bp, CDEIII = last 26 bp, by SGD's convention); **CDEII is everything between
   them**. Sequence and length run from the first base of CDEI to the last base of
   CDEIII, so insertions are kept and every strain is measured the same way.
5. **Align** each centromere's sequences together with the S288C element (MAFFT
   `--auto`); S288C is kept as a reference column, not counted as a strain.

```{r tbl-funnel}
#| tbl-cap: "From BLAST hits to one annotated locus per assembly and centromere."
cde_by_sample <- aligned |> group_by(sample) |> summarise(cde_ok = sum(cde_ok))
d$qc |>
  left_join(select(strains, sample, assembly), by = "sample") |>
  left_join(cde_by_sample, by = "sample") |>
  transmute(Assembly = assembly, `BLAST hits` = raw_hits,
            `Cross-centromere hits removed` = raw_hits - after_locus_assignment,
            `Split pieces merged` = after_locus_assignment - final_loci,
            `Final loci` = final_loci, `Confident CDEI + CDEIII` = cde_ok) |>
  arrange(Assembly) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
`r n_cross` of `r qc_tot[["raw_hits"]]` BLAST hits were another centromere's locus.
They are short (~90–100 bp) and weak (e ≈ 1e-6), but long enough to pass a
length filter, which is how an earlier analysis of 748 strains came to treat about
a third of its "CEN14" and "CEN15" sequences as the other centromere.

All `r n_loci` loci were found on the expected chromosome, including the
centromeres that sit on rearranged chromosomes. `r n_cde_ok` of `r n_loci` have both
CDEI and CDEIII scoring within 2 bits of the weakest S288C element; the exception
is listed in @tbl-cdeflag.
:::

```{r tbl-cdeflag}
#| tbl-cap: "Loci whose CDEI or CDEIII scored below the confidence threshold."
flag <- aligned |> filter(!cde_ok)
if (nrow(flag) == 0) {
  knitr::kable(tibble(Note = "None — every CDEI and CDEIII call is confident."))
} else {
  flag |> transmute(Assembly = assembly, Centromere = centromere, CDEI = cdei_seq,
                    `CDEI score` = cdei_score, CDEIII = cdeiii_seq,
                    `CDEIII score` = cdeiii_score, `Length, bp` = sequence_length) |>
    knitr::kable()
}
```

## Checked against the published atlas {#sec-validation}

```{r validation-load}
val_h_path <- file.path(params$data_dir, "validation_helsen.tsv")
val_p_path <- file.path(params$data_dir, "validation_pcan.tsv")
has_val <- file.exists(val_h_path) && file.exists(val_p_path)
if (has_val) {
  val_h <- read_tsv(val_h_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  val_p <- read_tsv(val_p_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  same  <- filter(val_h, source == "helsen_same_assembly")
  other <- filter(val_h, source == "helsen_other_assembly") |>
    left_join(select(strains, sample, assembly, zygosity), by = "sample")
  found <- filter(val_p, status == "found")
  n_same_id  <- sum(same$status == "identical")
  n_other_id <- sum(other$status == "identical")
  n_other_cmp <- sum(other$status != "absent_in_helsen")
  n_pcan_only <- sum(val_p$status == "pcan_only")
  pcan_d3 <- names(which.max(table(found$d3)))
}
```

```{r tbl-validation}
#| eval: !expr has_val
#| tbl-cap: "Our loci compared with three independent calls. Same assembly: Helsen et al. 2026 Supplementary Data 4 rows for the same GenBank accession, located in our contig. Other assembly: the Peter et al. 2018 short-read assembly of the same strain (sequence alignment; end gaps ignored). PCAn: Helsen's tool run here on our assemblies (Saccharomyces motifs, no synteny step)."
tibble(
  Check = c("Helsen SD4, same assembly", "Helsen SD4, Peter 2018 assembly of the strain", "PCAn v1.0 on our assemblies"),
  Loci = c(nrow(same), nrow(other), sum(val_p$status != "pcan_only")),
  `Called by them` = c(sum(same$status != "absent_in_helsen"), n_other_cmp, nrow(found)),
  `Identical to ours` = c(n_same_id, n_other_id, sum(found$d5 == 0 & found$d3 == as.integer(pcan_d3))),
  `Extra calls (theirs only)` = c("–", "–", as.character(n_pcan_only))
) |> knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
On the very same assemblies, Helsen's published atlas and our pipeline agree on
`r if (has_val) n_same_id else "–"` of `r if (has_val) nrow(same) else "–"` loci base for base,
CDEI start and CDEIII end included. Their sequences, and PCAn's, carry one base past the
SGD CDEIII end (checked on S288C, all 16); that constant offset is removed before comparing.
PCAn, run independently, finds the same loci and no others: it adds nothing as a
locator for these genomes, but confirms the CDE boundaries are not an artefact of
our S288C-trained PWMs.

The comparison with the Peter 2018 assemblies of the same strains is different in
kind: another isolate stock, short reads, a collapsed diploid. Differences there
fall almost entirely on heterozygous strains (@tbl-validation-strain), so they mostly
show which allele each assembly happened to keep, not errors on either side.
:::

```{r tbl-validation-strain}
#| eval: !expr has_val
#| tbl-cap: "Our ScRAP loci vs the Peter 2018 assembly of the same strain, per strain."
other |>
  group_by(Assembly = assembly, Zygosity = zygosity) |>
  summarise(Compared = sum(status != "absent_in_helsen"),
            Identical = sum(status == "identical"),
            SNVs = sum(snv, na.rm = TRUE), `Indel bp` = sum(indel_bp, na.rm = TRUE),
            `CDEII length differs` = sum(cdeii_diff != 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(Zygosity, Assembly) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r tbl-validation-cdeii}
#| eval: !expr has_val
#| tbl-cap: "Loci whose CDEII length differs by 3 bp or more between our assembly and the Peter 2018 assembly of the same strain."
other |>
  filter(abs(cdeii_diff) >= 3) |>
  transmute(Assembly = assembly, Zygosity = zygosity, Centromere = centromere,
            `CDEII ours, bp` = our_cdeii, `CDEII Peter 2018, bp` = our_cdeii + cdeii_diff,
            SNVs = snv, `Indel bp` = indel_bp) |>
  arrange(Assembly, Centromere) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Four locators, reconciled {#sec-locators}

```{r locators-load}
lc <- load_locators(params$data_dir)
has_lc <- !is.null(lc)
if (has_lc) {
  cat_n <- table(lc$rec$category)
  n_rec <- nrow(lc$rec)
  n_agree <- sum(lc$rec$category == "agree")
  n_bridged <- sum(lc$l3$status == "bridged")
  rearr <- aligned |> filter(grepl("_chr", contig_name)) |>
    left_join(lc$rec |> select(sample, centromere, category), by = c("sample", "centromere"))
  g0 <- lc$rounds |> group_by(round) |> summarise(n = sum(n_profile), ok = sum(found_ok), bits = mean(s288c_bits))
  near <- lc$nearest |>
    left_join(distinct(aligned, sseqid, contig_name), by = c(contig = "sseqid")) |>
    mutate(chrom = coalesce(contig_name, contig))
  n_near_chr9 <- sum(grepl("chrIX", near$chrom))
  syn <- lc$syn_detail |> select(case, locator, status) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = locator, values_from = status) |>
    left_join(lc$syn, by = "case")
  syn_of <- function(k, col) syn[[col]][syn$case == k]
}
```

Every locus in this report so far comes from one method: BLAST of the 16 S288C
centromeres (L1). A centromere too diverged for BLAST would simply be missing. Three
more locators, each failing in a different way, were run on the same assemblies and
reconciled with L1 per assembly and centromere.

| | Locator | Depends on | Fails when |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | BLAST of the S288C CEN, CDEs placed by PWM | CEN sequence close to S288C | CEN diverged, large insertion |
| L2 | BLAST of the 2 kb on each side | flanks conserved and next to the CEN | a rearrangement breakpoint near the CEN |
| L3 | minimap2 whole-genome alignment to S288C, CEN coordinates lifted over | collinearity around the CEN | flanks deleted or duplicated |
| L4 | one HMM per centromere, grown from the strains it finds | the population profile | the profile drifts (guarded by a 10-bit margin over every other profile and the CDE check) |

Loci that overlap on one contig form one cluster; the locators in it are the locus's
support. Categories: `agree` (every locator that ran found it), `rescued` (L1 missed it,
another found it; it enters the main table with CDEs placed in that window),
`sequence_only` (L1 or L4 found it, neither L2 nor L3 anchored it), `insertion` (an exact
L2 or L3 locus more than 30 bp longer than S288C; the main table takes that window),
`conflict` (loci on different contigs, listed, not resolved), `partial` and `missing`.

```{r tbl-locators}
#| eval: !expr has_lc
#| tbl-cap: "Each locator against L1 over all assembly × centromere pairs. Same boundaries: CDEI start and CDEIII end identical. L3 counts only exactly lifted loci there; bridged ones (the CEN inside an unaligned stretch between two collinear alignment blocks) cover the whole stretch."
locator_vs_l1(lc) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r tbl-locator-categories}
#| eval: !expr has_lc
#| tbl-cap: "Reconciled categories."
lc$rec |> count(Category = category, Support = support, name = "Loci") |> knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
All four locators find the same `r if (has_lc) n_agree else "–"` of
`r if (has_lc) n_rec else "–"` loci, nothing is rescued and nothing conflicts: in these
ten genomes BLAST missed no centromere. That includes the
`r if (has_lc) nrow(rearr) else "–"` centromeres sitting on translocated chromosomes
(`r if (has_lc) paste(unique(paste(rearr$assembly, rearr$contig_name)), collapse = ", ") else "–"`),
where synteny could have failed and did not. The boundary differences are small and
explained: L2 extrapolates past an indel at the edge of a flank, and L3 bridges
`r if (has_lc) n_bridged else "–"` centromeres that minimap2 left unaligned.
:::

```{r fig-hmm-growth}
#| eval: !expr has_lc
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-cap: "L4 grown from the S288C sequences alone. Grey: one line per centromere; blue: mean. Each round accepts a strain's sequence only when its own profile beats every other profile by ≥ 10 bits there and CDEI and CDEIII pass the PWM check; the loop stops when a round adds nothing."
p <- plot_hmm_growth(lc$rounds)
save_fig(p, "fig_l4_growth", 11, 3.6)
p
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
From one sequence per centromere the profiles grow to
`r if (has_lc) g0$n[g0$round == 1] else "–"` sequences after one round and
`r if (has_lc) max(g0$n) else "–"` after `r if (has_lc) max(g0$round) else "–"`, when no new
sequence passes and the loop stops; loci found with status ok go from
`r if (has_lc) g0$ok[1] else "–"` to `r if (has_lc) tail(g0$ok, 1) else "–"` of 160. The S288C
sequence scores higher against the grown profile than against itself alone
(`r if (has_lc) fmt(g0$bits[1]) else "–"` → `r if (has_lc) fmt(tail(g0$bits, 1)) else "–"` bits,
mean): a single-sequence profile cannot tell which positions are conserved, a population
profile can. Rejections for a too-close runner-up profile, the sign of a profile drifting
towards another centromere: `r if (has_lc) sum(lc$rounds$rejected_runner_up) else "–"`.
:::

### Planted centromeres

The real genomes test only agreement. To test rescue, one assembly
(`r if (has_lc) "ADS" else "–"`) was copied with its CEN5 damaged, and all four locators
were rerun on the copy.

```{r tbl-locator-synthetic}
#| eval: !expr has_lc
#| tbl-cap: "Planted CEN5 in ADS. cdeii_random: CDEII replaced by random 90 %-AT sequence of the same length; cde_mutated: also 2 substitutions in CDEI and 3 in CDEIII; insertion: a full Ty1 (LTR–INT–LTR, 5.9 kb) in the middle of CDEII. L4 uses the final profiles. Planted CDEs: the main-table locus has exactly the planted sequence, CDEI and CDEIII. The other 15 centromeres agree in every case."
syn |>
  transmute(Case = case, `Planted bp` = planted_length, L1, L2, L3, L4,
            Category = category, Support = support, `Main-table bp` = final_length,
            `CDEII bp` = final_cdeii, `CDE check` = ifelse(cde_ok, "pass", "fail"),
            `Planted CDEs` = ifelse(sequence_is_planted & cdei_is_planted & cdeiii_is_planted, "yes", "no")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
With CDEII scrambled, BLAST loses CEN5 and so does the HMM: its profile draws most of its
score from CDEII, and CDEIII alone reaches only E ≈ 0.2. The flank and synteny locators
still find the locus, and the CDEs placed in their window are exactly the planted ones, so
the rescue works and comes from L2 and L3, not L4: the HMM removes the S288C bias of BLAST
but still depends on the centromere's own sequence. With CDEI and CDEIII mutated as well
the locus is still rescued, but fails the CDE check and enters the table flagged. The
5.9-kb Ty1 is the case BLAST gets wrong rather than misses: L1 returns a
`r if (has_lc) lc$syn_detail$length[lc$syn_detail$case == "insertion" & lc$syn_detail$locator == "L1"] else "–"`-bp
piece, which the reconciled table replaces with the full
`r if (has_lc) syn_of("insertion", "final_length") else "–"`-bp locus from the flanks
(`r if (has_lc) syn_of("insertion", "insertion_bp") else "–"` bp longer than S288C).
:::

### CEN-like elements

The final profiles were also searched over every contig, and over the S288C genome, for
a second centromere: a hit with E ≤ 10^-5^, its profile ≥ 10 bits ahead of every other one,
CDEI and CDEIII passing, outside every known locus.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
There is none, in any of the ten assemblies or in S288C
(`r if (has_lc) nrow(lc$cen_like) else "–"` candidates). The strongest hit outside the
known loci is the same in every genome, on chromosome IX
(`r if (has_lc) n_near_chr9 else "–"` of `r if (has_lc) nrow(near) else "–"` genomes, about
70 kb from CEN9): a stretch matching the CEN15 profile at
E `r if (has_lc) signif(min(near$evalue), 2) else "–"`–`r if (has_lc) signif(max(near$evalue), 2) else "–"`
(`r if (has_lc) paste(range(near$bits), collapse = "–") else "–"` bits), in S288C on
`r if (has_lc) with(near[near$sample == "S288C", ], paste0(contig, ":", min(env_from, env_to))) else "–"`,
three to four orders of magnitude short of the threshold. No neocentromere, no dicentric
arm, no stray CEN fragment.
:::

## CDEII length in helical steps {#sec-cdeii-steps}

```{r microevo-load}
mev <- load_microevo(params$data_dir)
has_mev <- !is.null(mev)
if (has_mev) {
  st <- mev$steps
  var_loci <- filter(st, class_median != "within")
  hs <- filter(mev$h_steps, !divergent)
  n_h_asm <- sum(mev$h_steps$n_assemblies)
  h_by_d <- hs |> group_by(d = abs(delta_median)) |> summarise(n = sum(n_assemblies), .groups = "drop")
  h_n <- function(lo, hi) sum(h_by_d$n[h_by_d$d >= lo & h_by_d$d <= hi])
  n_col <- sum(mev$hap$verdict == "other_assembly_at_median")
}
```

CDEII is wrapped once around the Cse4 nucleosome, between Cbf1 on CDEI and CBF3 on
CDEIII. Adding or removing about one helical turn (~10 bp) keeps the two complexes on
the same face of the DNA; half a turn (~5 bp) rotates one relative to the other.
Helsen et al. 2026 found ~10-bp steps tolerated in natural strains and 5-bp steps not.
Here each CDEII is compared with the **population median** for its centromere, not with
S288C: the S288C CEN4 CDEII (77 bp) is itself an 8-bp deletion relative to almost every
other strain.

```{r fig-cdeii-steps}
#| eval: !expr has_mev
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "CDEII length of every locus relative to the median for its centromere (10 ScRAP assemblies plus S288C). Shaded: one and two helical turns (8–12, 18–22 bp); dashed lines: multiples of 10.2 bp. Labelled points are outside ±2 bp. Hover for the indels found against the reference allele."
p_steps <- plot_cdeii_steps(st)
save_fig(p_steps, "fig_b1_cdeii_steps", 10, 6)
as_plotly(p_steps, 560)
```

```{r tbl-cdeii-variants}
#| eval: !expr has_mev
#| tbl-cap: "Loci outside ±2 bp of the median, with indels of 3 bp or more against the reference allele (the most frequent CDEII sequence of median length), and what the Peter 2018 assembly of the same strain shows (Helsen SD4). `tandem x1u22 mh10` = one extra copy of a 22-bp unit with 10 bp of junction microhomology."
var_loci |>
  left_join(select(mev$hap, strain, centromere, phasing, other_assembly_cdeii, verdict),
            by = c("strain", "centromere")) |>
  transmute(Strain = strain, Centromere = as.character(centromere), `CDEII, bp` = cdeii_length,
            `Median, bp` = median_length, `Δ, bp` = delta_median, Class = class,
            `Indels ≥ 3 bp` = coalesce(events, "– (only 1–2 bp indels)"),
            Assembly = coalesce(phasing, "reference"),
            `Peter 2018 CDEII, bp` = coalesce(other_assembly_cdeii, "–"),
            Verdict = coalesce(verdict, "–")) |>
  arrange(Class, Strain) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
`r if (has_mev) sum(st$class_median == "within") else "–"` of
`r if (has_mev) nrow(st) else "–"` loci lie within ±2 bp of the median. The two
whole-turn variants are the CFS CEN16 tandem duplication (+22 bp, two turns) and S288C's
own CEN4 (−8 bp, a non-tandem 7-bp deletion plus 1 bp). The off-step loci are all
−3 to −5 bp, and `r if (has_mev) n_col else "–"` of them sit on collapsed (heterozygous)
assemblies or on ADS, where the Peter 2018 assembly of the same strain carries a CDEII of
median length. In a collapsed assembly that is what a heterozygote looks like: each
assembly kept a different haplotype. Without ScRAP reads (not local) this stays a
candidate, not a call. ADS is homozygous, so its CEN6 difference (80 vs 83 bp) is a
real disagreement between the two assemblies. The two remaining off-step loci, CEN13 in
ASN (−3) and BCE (−4), are the same 3-bp deletion and are found at the same length in
Peter 2018 as well: a real, shared short allele.
:::

### The same scan on the Helsen atlas

Every distinct CDEII in Helsen Supplementary Data 4 was run through the same indel
caller, weighted by the number of assemblies carrying it. Alleles aligning to the
reference at < 85 % identity (gap-free columns) are excluded: their alignments place
compensating insertion–deletion pairs that are not real events.

```{r fig-helsen-steps}
#| eval: !expr has_mev
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "CDEII length relative to the per-centromere median in Helsen SD4 (all centromeres pooled; log scale). Bands and lines as above."
p_hs <- plot_helsen_steps(mev$h_steps)
save_fig(p_hs, "fig_b2_helsen_steps", 10, 4.2)
as_plotly(p_hs, 400)
```

```{r tbl-helsen-recurrent}
#| eval: !expr has_mev
#| tbl-cap: "Recurrent CDEII variants in Helsen SD4: |Δ| ≥ 5 bp and carried by at least 3 assemblies."
hs |>
  filter(abs(delta_median) >= 5, n_assemblies >= 3) |>
  arrange(desc(n_assemblies)) |>
  transmute(Allele = allele, Assemblies = n_assemblies, `CDEII, bp` = cdeii_length,
            `Δ, bp` = delta_median, Class = class, `Indels ≥ 3 bp` = events) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
Over `r if (has_mev) format(n_h_asm, big.mark = ",") else "–"` CEN calls, half-turn
steps are close to absent: |Δ| = 5–7 bp in `r if (has_mev) h_n(5, 7) else "–"`
assemblies against `r if (has_mev) h_n(8, 12) else "–"` at 8–12 bp, while 3–4 bp
changes (mostly in A/T runs) are common (`r if (has_mev) h_n(3, 4) else "–"`). This fits
Helsen's model. Two recurrent variants fit it less well: CEN2 +13 bp and CEN3 +25 bp,
exact tandem duplications carried by dozens of assemblies, i.e. about 1.3 and 2.5 turns.
Whether those strains carry compensating changes elsewhere in the kinetochore is a
question for analysis C. All three large insertions (CEN2 +13, CEN16 +22, CEN3 +25) are
exact tandem duplications with 4–12 bp of junction microhomology, whereas the common
CEN4 −8 bp allele (the S288C one) is a non-tandem deletion.
:::

## Kinetochore genes {#sec-kinetochore}

```{r kinetochore-load}
kt <- load_kinetochore(params$data_dir)
has_kt <- !is.null(kt)
if (has_kt) {
  ktg <- filter(kt$genes, strain != "S288C")
  kt_ctrl <- filter(kt$genes, strain == "S288C")
  n_ctrl_ok <- sum(kt_ctrl$status == "intact" & kt_ctrl$n_substitutions == 0 & kt_ctrl$n_other_variants == 0)
  n_kt_strains <- n_distinct(ktg$strain)
  kt_fs <- filter(ktg, status != "intact")
  kt_shift <- filter(ktg, start_shift_codons > 0)
  kt_private <- filter(kt$positions, ref_private)
  cdei_fixed <- kt$cen |> filter(cde_ok) |> group_by(centromere) |>
    summarise(k = n_distinct(cdei_core), .groups = "drop")
  n_ccg <- sum(kt$cen$ccg_hit, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Strain pairs that carry the same haplotype at every gene
  hm <- select(kt$matrix, strain, all_of(KT_GENES))
  pairs <- combn(hm$strain, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  shared <- vapply(pairs, \(p) sum(unlist(hm[hm$strain == p[1], KT_GENES]) ==
                                   unlist(hm[hm$strain == p[2], KT_GENES])), integer(1))
  top_pair <- pairs[[which.max(shared)]]
}
```

The centromere is read by proteins, so a change in CDEI–CDEIII could be tolerated
because the proteins that bind it changed too. Ten kinetochore genes were extracted
from every assembly (`tblastn` with the S288C proteins, exons stitched, translated):
**Cbf1** on CDEI; the CBF3 complex on CDEIII (**Cep3**, whose Zn₂Cys₆ domain contacts
the `CCG`, **Ndc10**, **Ctf13**, **Skp1**); the centromeric histone **Cse4** and its
chaperone **Scm3**; and the inner kinetochore (**Mif2**, **Okp1**, **Ame1**). As a
control, the same search on the S288C genome (R64) returns
`r if (has_kt) n_ctrl_ok else "–"` of 10 genes identical to the reference protein.

```{r fig-kinetochore-matrix}
#| eval: !expr has_kt
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-cap: "Kinetochore protein haplotypes per strain. Colour is the number of amino-acid substitutions against S288C; the label is the haplotype (same label within a gene = identical protein; · = identical to S288C; fs = frameshift, red). Strains are ordered by Cbf1 haplotype. Hover for the substitutions."
p_ktm <- plot_kinetochore_matrix(kt$genes)
save_fig(p_ktm, "fig_c1_kinetochore_haplotypes", 10, 4.8)
as_plotly(p_ktm, 440)
```

```{r tbl-kinetochore-private}
#| eval: !expr has_kt
#| tbl-cap: "Positions where every intact strain allele differs from S288C, i.e. S288C carries the rare residue."
kt_private |>
  transmute(Gene = gene, Position = ref_pos, `S288C` = ref, Strains = alleles,
            `Strains with call` = n, Domain = na_if(domain, "-") |> coalesce("–")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r tbl-kinetochore-fs}
#| eval: !expr has_kt
#| tbl-cap: "Gene calls that are not a plain substituted protein. `q409(hp4)` = frameshift at codon 409 of the query, in a 4-bp homopolymer. Start shift = first in-frame Met downstream of the S288C start."
bind_rows(
  kt_fs |> transmute(Strain = strain, Gene = as.character(gene), Call = "Frameshift",
                     Detail = frameshifts, `Protein, aa` = protein_length, `S288C, aa` = ref_length),
  kt_shift |> transmute(Strain = strain, Gene = as.character(gene), Call = "Start shift",
                        Detail = paste0("starts at Met", start_shift_codons + 1),
                        `Protein, aa` = protein_length, `S288C, aa` = ref_length)
) |>
  left_join(select(strains, strain, assembly), by = c(Strain = "strain")) |>
  relocate(Assembly = assembly, .after = Strain) |>
  arrange(Call, Gene, Strain) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
Every strain has its own protein haplotype at most genes; only
`r if (has_kt) paste(top_pair, collapse = " and ") else "–"` share
`r if (has_kt) max(shared) else "–"` of 10. Cse4 and Skp1 are almost invariant (one
substitution each, both in ASN). Three positions are S288C-private: **Cbf1 C262R** lies
in the bHLH, the DNA-binding domain that reads CDEI, so it is the S288C protein, not the
strains, that is unusual there; Ndc10 K774Q and Ame1 L97P are outside annotated domains.
In `r if (has_kt) nrow(kt_shift) else "–"` strains the first Ndc10 start codon is lost
and the protein begins 11 or 14 codons downstream; the N-terminus of Ndc10 is not part of
its DNA-binding core, so this is likely tolerated.

All `r if (has_kt) nrow(kt_fs) else "–"` frameshifts sit in collapsed assemblies (ASN,
ANM) and in 4–5 bp homopolymers. That is the signature of residual consensus errors in a
merged heterozygous assembly, and the predicted products (e.g. a 67-aa Ame1, an 86-aa
Cep3) would remove essential proteins. Without the reads these are treated as
unresolved, and only intact alleles enter the domain analysis below.
:::

### Where the protein variation sits

```{r fig-kinetochore-domains}
#| eval: !expr has_kt
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Variable positions per 100 aa in each annotated region (UniProt; Cse4 helices and loop 1 mapped from histone H3), among intact alleles. S288C-private positions are not counted. Point size is the region length. Hover for counts."
p_ktd <- plot_domain_rates(kt$domains)
save_fig(p_ktd, "fig_c2_kinetochore_domains", 9, 9)
as_plotly(p_ktd, 820)
```

```{r tbl-kinetochore-cen}
#| eval: !expr has_kt
#| tbl-cap: "Centromere side of the comparison, per strain (16 centromeres each). CDEI / CDEIII: centromeres with any substitution against S288C. CDEII length: centromeres whose CDEII length differs from S288C; off-step: by 3–7 or 13–17 bp."
kt$matrix |>
  transmute(Strain = strain, `CDEI` = n_cdei_alt, `CDEII length` = n_cdeii_len_alt,
            `CDEII off-step` = n_cdeii_off_step, `CDEIII` = n_cdeiii_alt,
            `CDEIII CCG hit` = n_ccg_hit, `No CDE call` = n_no_cde_call) |>
  arrange(Strain) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
The DNA-binding parts are conserved. The Cse4 histone-fold, END and loop 1 carry no
substitution at all (Cse4's single change, V128I, is in the NLS); the Cep3 Zn₂Cys₆ and
the Mif2 AT hook are invariant; the Cbf1 bHLH differs only by the S288C-private C262R.
The variation is in the disordered regions: the Cbf1 N-terminal tail
(`r if (has_kt) kt$domains$n_substituted[kt$domains$gene == "CBF1" & kt$domains$domain == "N-terminal disordered tail"] else "–"`
variable positions), the Mif2 and Ndc10 disordered segments, Scm3 and Ctf13. The Cbf1
tail is the region that changed along with the centromeres in other budding yeasts.

On the DNA side, the targets of these proteins hardly move either. The CDEI core is the
same in all strains at
`r if (has_kt) sum(cdei_fixed$k == 1) else "–"` of 16 centromeres, and the `CCG` that Cep3
contacts in CDEIII is changed in `r if (has_kt) n_ccg else "–"` loci. The one CEN-side
difference shared by every strain, CEN4 CDEII +8 bp relative to S288C (@sec-cdeii-steps),
is again S288C-private. So no strain combines an unusual centromere with an unusual
DNA-binding domain, and there is nothing to co-vary here. With one haplotype per strain,
any pairing of a protein allele with a centromere allele is confounded with strain
relatedness at n = 10; a real association test needs the full ScRAP set or the
1,011-genome assemblies.
:::

## Aneuploidy and centromere alleles {#sec-aneuploidy}

```{r aneuploidy-load}
an <- load_aneuploidy(file.path(params$repo, "output/peter748"))
has_an <- !is.null(an)
if (has_an) {
  an_strains <- unique(an$calls$strain)
  an_meta <- filter(an$meta, strain %in% an_strains, !is.na(aneuploidies))
  n_an_set <- length(an_strains)
  n_an_status <- nrow(an_meta)
  n_an_aneu <- sum(an_meta$aneuploidies != "euploid")
  an_tested <- filter(an$assoc, tested, predictor %in% names(ANEU_PREDICTORS))
  n_an_chrom <- n_distinct(an_tested$chrom)
  fr0 <- function(a, n) pct(a / n)
  an_min <- slice_min(an_tested, perm_p, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  an_nons288c <- an$calls |> filter(n_complete > 0) |> group_by(centromere) |>
    summarise(f = mean(non_s288c), .groups = "drop")
}
```

If a centromere allele binds the kinetochore less well, the chromosome that carries it
should be missegregated more often, and strains that are aneuploid for that chromosome
should carry the allele more often than euploid strains. This is tested on a different
and much larger set than the rest of the report: the Peter et al. 2018 short-read
assemblies, `r if (has_an) n_an_set else "–"` strains with BLAST loci for the 16
centromeres, of which `r if (has_an) n_an_status else "–"` have an aneuploidy call in
Peter 2018 Table S1 (`r if (has_an) n_an_aneu else "–"` aneuploid for at least one
chromosome). Among the ten ScRAP strains only CFS is aneuploid, so the question cannot be
asked there.

Those assemblies are not available locally, so the loci are the BLAST hits only, without
CDE annotation. A locus counts when the hit reaches within 2 bp of both ends of the S288C
element (BLAST usually trims the first base of CEN1). Two allele classes are used per
strain and centromere: **not the major allele** (sequence differs from the most common
complete sequence of that centromere) and **length differs from the mode**. "Differs
from S288C" is not used: S288C is the minority allele at most centromeres (e.g.
`r if (has_an) pct(an_nons288c$f[an_nons288c$centromere == "CEN6"]) else "–"` of strains
differ at CEN6), as in @sec-cdeii-steps. The outcome for chromosome *k* is any gain or
loss of *k*; a chromosome is tested when at least 10 strains are aneuploid for it
(`r if (has_an) n_an_chrom else "–"` of 16). Clade is the confounder, since both
aneuploidy and centromere alleles are clade-structured: odds ratios come from conditional
logistic regression stratified by clade, and p-values from 10,000 permutations of the
allele within clades, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction over the tested chromosomes.

```{r fig-aneuploidy}
#| eval: !expr has_an
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-cap: "Odds of aneuploidy for chromosome *k* in strains carrying the variant allele at CEN*k*, within clade (conditional logit; 95 % CI, clipped to 0.01–100). Only chromosomes with ≥ 10 aneuploid strains. ×: not estimable, because no aneuploid strain (or every one) carries the variant. Hover for the counts and permutation p."
p_an <- plot_aneuploidy_or(an$assoc)
save_fig(p_an, "fig_g1_aneuploidy_or", 10, 4.6)
as_plotly(p_an, 420)
```

```{r tbl-aneuploidy}
#| eval: !expr has_an
#| tbl-cap: "Per tested chromosome: aneuploid strains (gain / loss) and how many carry each allele class at the chromosome's own centromere, against the same fraction in euploid strains. p: within-clade permutation; q: BH over tested chromosomes."
fr <- function(a, n) paste0(a, "/", n, " (", pct(a / n), ")")
an_tested |>
  left_join(an$counts, by = "chrom") |>
  mutate(predictor = ANEU_PREDICTORS[predictor]) |>
  select(chrom, centromere, set_gain, set_loss, n_aneuploid, predictor, aneu_variant, eu_variant, eu_ref, perm_p, perm_q) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = predictor, values_from = c(aneu_variant, eu_variant, eu_ref, perm_p, perm_q)) |>
  arrange(chrom) |>
  transmute(Centromere = centromere, `Gain / loss` = paste(set_gain, "/", set_loss),
            `Major: aneuploid` = fr(`aneu_variant_Not the major allele`, n_aneuploid),
            `Major: euploid` = fr(`eu_variant_Not the major allele`,
                                  `eu_variant_Not the major allele` + `eu_ref_Not the major allele`),
            `Major: p` = signif(`perm_p_Not the major allele`, 2),
            `Length: aneuploid` = fr(`aneu_variant_Length differs from mode`, n_aneuploid),
            `Length: euploid` = fr(`eu_variant_Length differs from mode`,
                                   `eu_variant_Length differs from mode` + `eu_ref_Length differs from mode`),
            `Length: p` = signif(`perm_p_Length differs from mode`, 2),
            q = signif(pmin(`perm_q_Not the major allele`, `perm_q_Length differs from mode`), 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
Nothing comes out. No chromosome shows an association at either allele class: the
smallest permutation p is `r if (has_an) signif(an_min$perm_p, 2) else "–"`
(`r if (has_an) paste(an_min$centromere, ANEU_PREDICTORS[an_min$predictor]) else "–"`), and
all q are close to 1. Gains dominate (chromosomes I, IX, VIII, III and XI, as in
Peter 2018), and the variant fractions in aneuploid strains sit within sampling noise of
the euploid fractions, in both directions. Several length tests are not estimable because
no aneuploid strain carries a length variant at all, which also argues against a large
effect. The one raw difference shows why the clade
stratification matters: at CEN6, `r if (has_an) with(filter(an_tested, centromere == "CEN6", predictor == "length_variant"), fr0(aneu_variant, n_aneuploid)) else "–"`
of aneuploid strains carry a length variant against
`r if (has_an) with(filter(an_tested, centromere == "CEN6", predictor == "length_variant"), fr0(eu_variant, eu_variant + eu_ref)) else "–"`
of euploid ones (Fisher p ≈ 0.04 without clade), but within clades the odds ratio is
about 1: the aneuploid strains and the length allele come from the same clades.

This is a weak test, not evidence of absence. With
`r if (has_an) paste(min(an_tested$n_aneuploid), "to", max(an_tested$n_aneuploid)) else "–"`
aneuploid strains per chromosome only large odds ratios (roughly 3 or more) could be
detected. Aneuploidy is also unstable over a few hundred generations, so the call reflects
the isolate's recent history as much as its centromere. And the allele classes pool many
different sequences regardless of where the difference lies; without CDE annotation a
change in CDEII flanks counts the same as one in the CDEIII `CCG`. A sharper version would
restrict the variant class to CDEII length off a helical step or to CDEI/CDEIII changes,
which needs the CDE annotation and therefore the assemblies themselves.
:::
