## Centromere alleles and phenotypes {#sec-phenotypes}

```{r phenotypes-load}
ph <- load_phenotypes(file.path(params$repo, "output/peter748/phenotypes"))
has_ph <- !is.null(ph)
if (has_ph) {
  ph_all <- bind_rows(ph$primary, ph$secondary)
  ph_lambda <- ph_all |> distinct(family, lambda_family) |>
    mutate(label = PHENO_FAMILIES[family]) 
  lam <- function(f) signif(ph_lambda$lambda_family[ph_lambda$family == f], 2)
  n_tests <- function(d) sum(!is.na(d$p))
  ph_n_strains <- n_distinct(ph$predictors$strain[!is.na(ph$predictors$rare_burden)])
  ph_n_growth <- median(ph$samples$n[ph$samples$klass == "growth"])
  ph_n_expr <- median(ph$samples$n[ph$samples$klass == "expression"])
  ph_min_q <- min(ph$primary$q, na.rm = TRUE)
  ph_min_q2 <- min(ph$secondary$q, na.rm = TRUE)
  cup1 <- filter(ph$controls, grepl("CUP1", control))
  cnv_ctrl <- filter(ph$controls, grepl("own expression", control))
}
```

If a centromere allele segregates its chromosome less faithfully, the cost should show
most under drugs that stress the spindle or the replication fork, and an allele could also
act locally on the genes around it. This section asks both questions on the phenotypes of
Loegler et al. 2025 (`Phenotypes_8391Traits`: 241 growth conditions, RNA-seq and protein
abundance), with centromere alleles taken from the Helsen et al. 2026 atlas for the Peter
2018 genomes: `r if (has_ph) ph_n_strains else "–"` strains with all 16 centromeres
called, of which a median of `r if (has_ph) ph_n_growth else "–"` have a given growth trait
and `r if (has_ph) ph_n_expr else "–"` a given expression trait.

Four predictors, all relative to the population and not to S288C (@sec-cdeii-steps):
**not the major allele** at a centromere (0, ½ or 1 by the share of the strain's
haplotypes), **CDEII length difference** from that centromere's median, **off a helical
step** (|Δ| ≥ 3 bp and not within 2 bp of 10 or 20), and a genome-wide **rare-allele
burden** (centromeres carrying an allele below 5 % frequency). A per-centromere predictor is
tested only when at least 20 strains are in the minority class.

Relatedness is the main confounder, as in @sec-aneuploidy, so every test is a linear mixed
model (EMMAX: variance components fitted once per trait under the null, then a GLS Wald test
per predictor) with a kinship matrix from the 82,869 SNPs of the Peter 2018 GWAS matrix.
For a centromere on chromosome *k* the kinship leaves chromosome *k* out, so markers linked
to the centromere cannot absorb its effect. Ploidy and the copy change of chromosome *k*
(Peter 2018) are covariates. Traits are rank-inverse-normal transformed. Tests are split into
a **primary** family, fixed in advance (growth on benomyl, 4-NQO, hydroxyurea and
camptothecin; expression and protein of genes within 10 kb of the centromere against that
centromere; expression and protein of 11 kinetochore genes against every centromere and the
burden), and a **secondary** scan of all growth traits, each with its own BH correction.

```{r fig-phenotypes-qq}
#| eval: !expr has_ph
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-cap: "Observed against expected −log10 p per family of tests. Points on the diagonal: no association beyond chance. Hover for the trait, centromere, effect and, for the smallest p, the p after conditioning on the local haplotype."
p_ph <- plot_pheno_qq(ph$primary, ph$secondary)
save_fig(p_ph, "fig_p1_pheno_qq", 11, 3.6)
as_plotly(p_ph, 360)
```

```{r tbl-phenotypes-top}
#| eval: !expr has_ph
#| tbl-cap: "Smallest p in the primary family. β: change in the inverse-normal trait per unit of the predictor (per bp for CDEII Δ). p | local: the same test with 5 principal components of the SNPs within ±50 kb of the centromere added as covariates. q: BH over the primary family."
ph$primary |>
  slice_min(p, n = 12, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(Family = PHENO_FAMILIES[family], Trait = trait, Centromere = centromere,
            Predictor = PHENO_PREDICTORS[predictor], n, Minority = n_minor,
            β = signif(beta, 2), p = signif(p, 2), `p | local` = signif(p_local, 2), q = signif(q, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r tbl-phenotypes-controls}
#| eval: !expr has_ph
#| tbl-cap: "Positive controls run through the same model with the full kinship: CUP1 copy number (Peter 2018 CNV marker YHR055C) against growth on copper, and the five most variable ORF copy-number markers against the expression of the same ORF."
ph$controls |>
  transmute(Control = control, Trait = trait, Marker = marker, n, β = signif(beta, 2), p = signif(p, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
No association survives correction. The smallest q is
`r if (has_ph) signif(ph_min_q, 2) else "–"` in the primary family
(`r if (has_ph) n_tests(ph$primary) else "–"` tests) and
`r if (has_ph) signif(ph_min_q2, 2) else "–"` in the secondary scan
(`r if (has_ph) n_tests(ph$secondary) else "–"` tests). The model itself is not the reason:
CUP1 copy number comes out at p down to
`r if (has_ph) format(min(cup1$p), digits = 2) else "–"` for copper growth, and gene copy number
predicts the gene's own expression in
`r if (has_ph) sum(cnv_ctrl$p < 1e-10) else "–"` of `r if (has_ph) nrow(cnv_ctrl) else "–"`
control genes, with the expected positive sign. The growth family is well calibrated
(λ = `r if (has_ph) lam("primary_growth") else "–"`; secondary λ =
`r if (has_ph) lam("secondary") else "–"`).

The cis family is inflated (λ = `r if (has_ph) lam("primary_cis") else "–"`), almost
entirely in "not the major allele". That is expected rather than a failure of the
correction: the kinship deliberately leaves the centromere's chromosome out, so any
expression QTL near the centromere that travels on the same haplotype shows up as a
centromere effect. A centromere and a cis-eQTL 5 kb away cannot be separated with short-range
linkage this strong, and none of these tests reaches q < 0.05 anyway.

The most consistent growth signal is CDEII length at CEN11, with the same sign across
benomyl, anisomycin and DMSO at 40–48 h (YPD-based conditions). It is carried by small
groups (about 40 strains each at −1 and +1 bp, concentrated in the French Guiana and
Mosaic 3 clades), it does not weaken when the local haplotype is conditioned on, and it is
not specific to spindle stress. The lifted tail of the growth panel is mostly this one
signal repeated over six benomyl traits (two doses × three time points) measured on the
same strains, not independent hits. A 1-bp change in an AT-rich CDEII is the kind of
homopolymer length difference short-read assemblies get wrong, so this is a candidate to
check on long-read assemblies, not a finding. The same applies to the CEN4 −8 bp allele
(the S288C length class) with hydroxyurea and fluconazole.

In short: within the power of ~750 strains, natural centromere alleles have no detectable
effect on growth under segregation stress or on nearby and kinetochore gene expression.
With a minority class of 20–100 strains, effects of roughly 0.4 SD or more would have been
seen; smaller effects, or effects confined to rare alleles carried by a handful of strains,
cannot be excluded.
:::

---

## Transposons around centromeres {#sec-transposons}

```{r te-load}
te <- load_transposons(params$data_dir)
has_te <- !is.null(te)
if (has_te) {
  te_genomes <- sort(unique(te$elements$genome))
  te_counts <- te$elements |> count(genome)
  s288c_el <- filter(te$elements, genome == "S288C")
  chk_miss <- filter(te$check, !recovered)
  te_null_g <- filter(te$null, genome != "all", null == "tRNA-matched")
  te_pool <- filter(te$null, genome == "all")
  pool_of <- function(nl, w, col) te_pool[[col]][te_pool$null == nl & te_pool$window_kb == w]
  te_poly <- filter(te$sites, polymorphic)
  te_near5 <- te$summary |> group_by(centromere) |>
    summarise(n_with = sum(n_5kb > 0), te = median(nearest_te), trna = median(nearest_trna), .groups = "drop")
  all5 <- te_near5$centromere[te_near5$n_with == length(te_genomes)]
  cfa5 <- filter(te$near, genome == "CFA", centromere == "CEN5", distance <= 1000)
  cfa5_gap <- te$calls |> filter(source_genome == "CFA", centromere == "CEN5", call == "absent") |>
    pull(gap)
}
```

Point centromeres descend from Ty5 LTRs (Haase 2026), and Ty1 and Ty3 integrate upstream
of tRNA genes. That raises two questions for the strains here: are Ty elements and solo
LTRs closer to centromeres than expected, and are any of them insertions that only some
strains carry? Every Ty1–Ty5 element and solo LTR was annotated in the ten assemblies and
S288C. The queries were the internal region of one S288C element per family and all
`r if (has_te) sum(grepl("^LTR", names(read_fasta(file.path(params$repo, "data/ty_reference.fasta"))))) else "–"`
full-length S288C LTRs (SGD), searched with BLAST. A hit counts when it covers ≥ 70 % of a
query at ≥ 80 % identity. Abutting hits are joined into one element: a full element (≥ 70 %
of the internal region present), a truncated one, or a solo LTR. This gives
`r if (has_te) paste(min(te_counts$n), "to", max(te_counts$n)) else "–"` elements per
genome. On S288C, all 50 annotated Ty elements and all full-length LTRs are recovered.
`r if (has_te) nrow(chk_miss) else "–"` of the `r if (has_te) nrow(te$check) else "–"`
SGD features within 20 kb of a centromere are missed, all of them LTR fragments of
`r if (has_te) paste(min(chk_miss$length), "to", max(chk_miss$length)) else "–"` bp, below
the 70 % rule.

```{r fig-te-map}
#| eval: !expr has_te
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-cap: "Ty elements (bars: full or truncated) and solo LTRs (dots) within ±20 kb of each centromere, coloured by family; grey ticks are tRNA genes. Coordinates are oriented so the CDEI side is on the left. Hover for coordinates, distance and strand."
p_te <- plot_te_map(te$near, te$trna, te_genomes)
save_fig(p_te, "fig_d1_te_map", 12, 10)
as_plotly(p_te, 900)
```

Being near a centromere is only meaningful against a null that respects how Ty elements
choose where to insert. For each genome, 1,000 random positions were drawn, about 62 per
centromere. Each position matches that centromere's distance to the nearest tRNA gene
(±10 %) and lies at least 20 kb from contig ends and from every centromere. The statistic
is the number of elements within ±1, ±5 and ±20 kb summed over the 16 centromeres; the
null distribution is 10,000 such sums, each built from one matched position per
centromere. A uniform null (no tRNA matching) is shown next to it.

```{r fig-te-null}
#| eval: !expr has_te
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-cap: "Elements near the 16 centromeres of each genome (dot) against the tRNA-matched and uniform nulls (5–95 % bars, + = mean). Hover for p."
p_tn <- plot_te_null(te$null)
save_fig(p_tn, "fig_d2_te_null", 11, 4.8)
as_plotly(p_tn, 440)
```

```{r tbl-te-sites}
#| eval: !expr has_te
#| tbl-cap: "Insertion sites near a centromere that are present in some strains and empty in others, decided at the orthologous position. The 300 bp on each side of the element are searched in every other genome: flanks that abut = empty site, flanks around an annotated element = present. Unresolved: a flank has no unique hit; gap_no_te: the flanks enclose sequence that is not a called element (usually an LTR fragment)."
te_poly |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(Present = paste(te_genomes[startsWith(c_across(all_of(te_genomes)), "present")], collapse = ", "),
         Element = paste(unique(sub("^present:", "", c_across(all_of(te_genomes))[
           startsWith(c_across(all_of(te_genomes)), "present")])), collapse = "; "),
         Other = paste(te_genomes[!startsWith(c_across(all_of(te_genomes)), "present") &
                                    c_across(all_of(te_genomes)) != "absent"], collapse = ", ")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(factor(centromere, levels = CEN_LEVELS), distance) |>
  transmute(Centromere = centromere, `Distance (bp)` = distance, Side = side, Element, Present,
            `Empty in` = n_absent, `Not decided` = Other) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
**No enrichment that survives the right null.** In no single genome does the count
near the centromeres leave the tRNA-matched null at any window (smallest p
`r if (has_te) signif(min(te_null_g$p), 2) else "–"`). Summed over the 11 genomes, ±5 kb
holds `r if (has_te) pool_of("tRNA-matched", 5, "observed") else "–"` elements against
`r if (has_te) fmt(pool_of("tRNA-matched", 5, "null_mean")) else "–"` expected, and the
count is above the null mean in `r if (has_te) pool_of("tRNA-matched", 5, "genomes_above_null") else "–"`
of 11 genomes. The genomes are not independent replicates, though: most of these elements
are shared by descent, so the same insertion is counted up to eleven times. The
consistency reflects shared history, and the pooled p-value is not reported as a result.
The tRNA matching matters. Uniform positions would put the ±20 kb count at
`r if (has_te) round(pool_of("tRNA-matched", 20, "observed") / pool_of("uniform", 20, "null_mean"), 1) else "–"`×
expectation; matched positions bring it to
`r if (has_te) round(pool_of("tRNA-matched", 20, "ratio"), 1) else "–"`×. Centromeres sit
closer to tRNA genes than random positions do, and the nearest element is usually the one
by the nearest tRNA (median nearest element vs nearest tRNA:
`r if (has_te) with(filter(te_near5, centromere == "CEN14"), paste0(fmt(te / 1000), " vs ", fmt(trna / 1000), " kb")) else "–"`
at CEN14, `r if (has_te) with(filter(te_near5, centromere == "CEN16"), paste0(fmt(te / 1000), " vs ", fmt(trna / 1000), " kb")) else "–"`
at CEN16). Every genome has an element within 5 kb of
`r if (has_te) paste(all5, collapse = ", ") else "–"`, and each of these is the same
tRNA-associated insertion in all strains. Right at the centromere, elements are scarce:
one within 1 kb in all 176 loci, against
`r if (has_te) fmt(pool_of("uniform", 1, "null_mean")) else "–"` expected under the uniform
null but `r if (has_te) fmt(pool_of("tRNA-matched", 1, "null_mean")) else "–"` under the
matched one. That is too few to call a depletion.

**Polymorphic insertions.** `r if (has_te) nrow(te_poly) else "–"` of the
`r if (has_te) nrow(te$sites) else "–"` sites within 20 kb of a centromere are present in
some strains and empty in others; most are carried by one or two strains. The closest is a
solo Ty1 LTR in CFA, `r if (has_te && nrow(cfa5)) cfa5$distance[1] else "–"` bp from
CEN5 on the CDEI side. In CFA the LTR is flanked on both sides by `CTACA`, the 5-bp
target-site duplication Ty1 makes; in the other ten genomes the two flanks abut with a
single copy (overlap `r if (has_te && length(cfa5_gap)) paste(unique(abs(cfa5_gap)), collapse = "–") else "–"` bp
by BLAST, whose element boundary here includes one base of the duplication). So this is
a recent insertion in CFA, not a deletion in the others. CFA's CEN5 itself is unchanged (@sec-cdeii-steps), so an
LTR this close does not disrupt the CDE. Whether it affects chromosome V segregation is
not something this data can answer. At one CEN11 site, CNT carries a full Ty1 where other
strains have a solo LTR, the expected product of LTR–LTR recombination excising the
internal region. The only Loegler 2025 structural-variant hotspot that reaches a
centromere is `r if (has_te && nrow(te$s5)) paste0("region ", te$s5$region[1], " (", te$s5$type[1], ", chrIII ", te$s5$start[1] / 1000, "–", te$s5$end[1] / 1000, " kb)") else "–"`,
which spans CEN3 and is flagged for Ty, LTR and tRNA content. CEN3 also has the most
polymorphic sites here (`r if (has_te) sum(te_poly$centromere == "CEN3") else "–"`).

Limits: ten genomes, so a site seen in one strain is a single observation. LTR fragments
below the 70 % rule are not counted (they show up as `gap_no_te`). A flank that falls in
repeated sequence leaves the site undecided rather than called.
:::

---

## CDE-like motifs in Ty LTRs {#sec-ltr-cde}

```{r lc-load}
lc <- load_ltr_cde(params$data_dir)
has_lc <- !is.null(lc)
if (has_lc) {
  lc_uniq <- distinct(lc$scores, seq_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  lc_ctl <- lc$control
  ctl_of <- function(ctrl, set, motif, col) lc_ctl[[col]][lc_ctl$control == ctrl & lc_ctl$set == set & lc_ctl$motif == motif]
  lc_pos_miss <- filter(lc$pos, !found)
  lc_off_cen <- filter(lc$units, is.na(centromere))
  lc_units_g <- count(lc$units, genome)
  lc_shuf_fam <- filter(lc_ctl, control == "shuffled", motif == "cdei", set != "unique LTRs (all)")
  lc_gen_g <- filter(lc_ctl, control == "genomic", motif == "cdei", set != "all genomes LTRs")
  lc_bce <- filter(lc_gen_g, set == "BCE LTRs")
  lc_max3 <- max(lc_uniq$best_cdeiii)
}
```

If point centromeres descend from Ty5 LTRs (Haase 2026), present-day LTRs might still
carry CDE-like motifs: dormant proto-centromeres. Every LTR from @sec-transposons was
scanned on both strands with the CDEI and CDEIII matrices used for the CDE annotation.
That is `r if (has_lc) nrow(lc$scores) else "–"` LTRs: the solo LTRs plus both LTRs of
each full element, `r if (has_lc) nrow(lc_uniq) else "–"` distinct sequences. A *hit* scores
at least as well as the weakest S288C element minus 2 (CDEI ≥
`r if (has_lc) lc$thr$cdei_min else "–"`, CDEIII ≥ `r if (has_lc) lc$thr$cdeiii_min else "–"`).
A *unit* is a CDEI hit followed on the same strand by a CDEII-like spacer
(`r if (has_lc) paste0(lc$thr$cdeii_min_len, "–", lc$thr$cdeii_max_len) else "–"` bp, AT ≥
`r if (has_lc) lc$thr$cdeii_min_at else "–"`; S288C has 77–86 bp and 0.86–0.98) and then a
CDEIII hit. CDEI's core CACRTG is an ordinary E-box, so counts are only meaningful against
a background. Three were used: `r if (has_lc) lc$thr$n_shuffles else "–"` dinucleotide-preserving
shuffles of each distinct LTR; windows of the same lengths drawn at random from each genome,
avoiding Ty elements, tRNA genes and the centromeres ±1 kb; and, for S288C only, the same
windows restricted to gene-free sequence (SGD annotation),
`r if (has_lc) lc$thr$n_resamples else "–"` window sets each. The scanner was first run on
the centromeres themselves. It finds a unit at `r if (has_lc) sum(lc$pos$found) else "–"` of
`r if (has_lc) nrow(lc$pos) else "–"` loci, with the same CDEII as the CDE annotation. The
two it misses fall outside the definitions:
`r if (has_lc) paste(paste(lc_pos_miss$genome, lc_pos_miss$centromere), collapse = " and ") else "–"`
(CDEIII just under the threshold, and a 105-bp CDEII with the 22-bp tandem duplication from
@sec-cdeii-steps).

```{r fig-ltr-cde}
#| eval: !expr has_lc
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-cap: "Best CDEI and CDEIII score in each sequence: distinct Ty LTRs, one dinucleotide shuffle of each, and one set of random genomic windows of matched length. Dashed: hit threshold. Ticks: the scores of the 160 ScRAP centromere loci."
p_lc <- plot_ltr_cde_scores(lc)
save_fig(p_lc, "fig_e1_ltr_cde_scores", 11, 4.4)
as_plotly(p_lc, 420)
```

```{r tbl-ltr-cde}
#| eval: !expr has_lc
#| tbl-cap: "Motif hits per kb in LTRs against each background. Shuffled: distinct LTR sequences; genomic and intergenic: all LTRs of the genome(s). Null: mean and 95 % range of the background; p: empirical two-sided (shuffles: 100 replicates, so p ≥ 0.02); q: BH within each background."
lc_ctl |>
  filter(set %in% c("unique LTRs (all)", "all genomes LTRs", "S288C LTRs")) |>
  transmute(Background = control, Set = set, Motif = c(cdei = "CDEI", cdeiii = "CDEIII", units = "Unit")[motif],
            Observed = obs, `Per kb` = obs_per_kb, `Null per kb` = null_mean_per_kb,
            `Null 95 %` = paste0(null_q025, "–", null_q975), Ratio = ratio,
            p = signif(p, 2), q = signif(q, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
**No proto-centromeres in the LTRs.** Not one LTR contains a unit, and not one contains
a CDEIII hit (best CDEIII score in any LTR `r if (has_lc) fmt(lc_max3, 2) else "–"`, against a
threshold of `r if (has_lc) lc$thr$cdeiii_min else "–"`). The genome-wide scan explains why
this is not a matter of the threshold: across the 11 genomes, units occur
`r if (has_lc) nrow(lc$units) else "–"` times and
`r if (has_lc) nrow(lc_off_cen) else "–"` of them lie outside a centromere. That is
`r if (has_lc) paste(sort(unique(lc_units_g$n)), collapse = " or ") else "–"` per genome, one
per centromere, minus the two loci above. CDEIII-scoring 26-mers are themselves rare
away from centromeres (null
`r if (has_lc) format(ctl_of("genomic", "all genomes LTRs", "cdeiii", "null_mean_per_kb"), scientific = FALSE) else "–"`
per kb in random genomic windows,
`r if (has_lc) format(ctl_of("intergenic", "S288C LTRs", "cdeiii", "null_mean_per_kb"), scientific = FALSE) else "–"`
in S288C gene-free sequence), and the full unit picks out centromeres alone.

**CDEI-like sites are depleted, not enriched.** LTRs carry
`r if (has_lc) fmt(ctl_of("shuffled", "unique LTRs (all)", "cdei", "obs_per_kb"), 2) else "–"`
CDEI hits per kb against
`r if (has_lc) fmt(ctl_of("shuffled", "unique LTRs (all)", "cdei", "null_mean_per_kb"), 2) else "–"`
in their own shuffles (ratio `r if (has_lc) ctl_of("shuffled", "unique LTRs (all)", "cdei", "ratio") else "–"`).
The ratio is below 1 in every family
(`r if (has_lc) paste0(sub("unique LTRs \\((.*)\\)", "\\1", lc_shuf_fam$set), " ", lc_shuf_fam$ratio, collapse = ", ") else "–"`),
and the observed rate lies outside the shuffle range in all of them. With 100 shuffles,
p cannot fall below 0.02, so the BH q of 0.06 reflects the replicate count rather than
the size of the effect. Against random genomic windows the ratio is
`r if (has_lc) ctl_of("genomic", "all genomes LTRs", "cdei", "ratio") else "–"` (all genomes)
and `r if (has_lc) ctl_of("intergenic", "S288C LTRs", "cdei", "ratio") else "–"` against S288C
gene-free sequence. Most of the hits are one site, about 40–60 bp into the Ty1 delta LTR
(`ATCAYATG`). The exception is
BCE: its LTRs have `r if (has_lc) lc_bce$ratio else "–"`× the genomic rate, because many
of its Ty1 solo LTRs carry the exact `ATCACATG` variant at that position (70 in BCE, 13 in
S288C). This looks like a delta subfamily specific to BCE. It is a CDEI-like E-box, with
nothing CDEII- or CDEIII-like downstream.

So LTRs in today's *S. cerevisiae* hold no remnant CDE layout. A Ty5 origin of point
centromeres (Haase 2026) would be much older than any LTR here. Within this species, a
CEN-like hit that lands in an LTR would be new, not inherited. The candidate list for
the locator's CEN-like scan is therefore empty, and any LTR hit there should be reported
as such.

Limits: thresholds are tied to the 16 S288C elements, so a degenerate ancestral CDE would
fall below them. The figure shows the score distributions, not only the calls. Diverged
LTR fragments below the 70 % rule of @sec-transposons were not scanned.
:::

---

## Diversity at the centromere and its flanks {#sec-diversity}

```{r dv-load}
dv <- load_diversity(params$data_dir)
has_dv <- !is.null(dv)
if (has_dv) {
  dv_pool <- filter(dv$summary, centromere == "all")
  dv_per <- filter(dv$summary, centromere != "all")
  pool <- function(el, col) dv_pool[[col]][dv_pool$element == el]
  dv_br <- filter(dv$l3, status == "bridged")
  dv_ex <- filter(dv$l3, status == "lifted")
  dv_fl <- dv$win |> filter(!region %in% ELEMENTS) |> mutate(k = abs(offset))
  dv_k <- dv_fl |> group_by(k) |> summarise(pi = median(pi), pi_sub = median(pi_sub), .groups = "drop")
  dv_far <- dv_fl |> filter(k >= 10) |> group_by(centromere) |> summarise(far = median(pi))
  dv_k1_above <- dv_fl |> filter(k == 1) |> left_join(dv_far, by = "centromere") |> summarise(sum(pi > far)) |> pull()
  dv_cc_bad <- filter(dv$cross, abs(rel_diff) > 0.10)
}
```

Is a centromere more or less variable than the DNA around it? Each S288C centromere ±2 kb
was carried over to every assembly through a whole-genome alignment (minimap2, `asm5`)
and our own liftover of its `cs` string. The 11 windows per centromere were aligned with
MAFFT, and every column was given its S288C position. Columns were then split into
CDEI, CDEII, CDEIII (S288C boundaries) and 20 windows of 100 bp on each side. π is the mean
over sequence pairs of differences per comparable site. A pair counts a substitution
per differing base and one event per indel, whatever its length. Truncated ends count
as missing, not as indels. π~sub~ and the indel rate are the two parts.

The liftover placed `r if (has_dv) sum(dv$l3$agree, na.rm = TRUE) else "–"` of
`r if (has_dv) nrow(dv$l3) else "–"` loci on the same contig as the BLAST + CDE locus.
`r if (has_dv) nrow(dv_ex) else "–"` lift base-to-base (both ends within
`r if (has_dv) max(abs(c(dv_ex$d_start, dv_ex$d_end))) else "–"` bp).
At the other `r if (has_dv) nrow(dv_br) else "–"`
(`r if (has_dv) paste(paste(dv_br$strain, dv_br$centromere), collapse = ", ") else "–"`),
minimap2 breaks its alignment at the centromere itself and resumes after it, on the same
contig and strand. These are bridged: the window is taken across the gap, and MAFFT
aligns it. CEN6 is unaligned in 6 of 10 assemblies, so `asm5` alone would lose the most
variable sequence. All 160 windows lifted at full ±2 kb. As a check, CEN π from these
window alignments matches the CEN-only alignment of @sec-variants within 10 % at
`r if (has_dv) sum(abs(dv$cross$rel_diff) <= 0.10) else "–"` of 16 centromeres.
`r if (has_dv && nrow(dv_cc_bad)) paste0("The exception, ", dv_cc_bad$centromere, " (", round(100 * dv_cc_bad$rel_diff), " %), comes entirely from how the two alignments place ", dv_cc_bad$explained_by, "'s indels: without ", dv_cc_bad$explained_by, " the difference is ", signif(100 * dv_cc_bad$rel_diff_without, 1), " %.") else ""`

```{r fig-pi-profile}
#| eval: !expr has_dv
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Nucleotide diversity along each centromere ±2 kb (11 genomes). Grey: one line per centromere, 100-bp windows; black: median. The shaded band is the centromere, drawn at a fixed width, with one point per centromere for each element and the median as a bar. √ scale, so zeros stay visible. Hover for the substitution and indel parts."
p_dv <- plot_pi_profile(dv)
save_fig(p_dv, "fig_f1_pi_profile", 11, 5)
as_plotly(p_dv, 480)
```

```{r tbl-diversity}
#| eval: !expr has_dv
#| tbl-cap: "π per element against the flanks, over 16 centromeres. Flank: mean over the 40 flank windows of that centromere. Below flank: centromeres where the element's π is lower. p: Wilcoxon signed-rank test, element vs flank mean, 16 pairs (the one test of this section)."
dv_pool |>
  transmute(Element = element, `Median π` = signif(median_pi, 2), `Median flank π` = signif(median_flank_pi, 2),
            `Below flank` = paste0(n_below_flank_pi, " / ", n_cen),
            `Median π subst.` = signif(median_pi_sub, 2), `Median indel rate` = signif(median_indel_rate, 2),
            `Flank indel rate` = signif(median_flank_indel_rate, 2), p = signif(wilcoxon_p, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
**CDEII is the most variable sequence in the region.** Its median π
(`r if (has_dv) signif(pool("CDEII", "median_pi"), 2) else "–"`) is about
`r if (has_dv) round(pool("CDEII", "median_pi") / pool("CDEII", "median_flank_pi")) else "–"`×
the flank mean. It is higher at every centromere, and above every one of its own 40 flank
windows at `r if (has_dv) sum(dv_per$element == "CDEII" & dv_per$percentile_pi == 100) else "–"`
of 16. Substitutions make most of it. The indel rate
(`r if (has_dv) signif(pool("CDEII", "median_indel_rate"), 2) else "–"` per site) is
`r if (has_dv) round(pool("CDEII", "median_indel_rate") / pool("CDEII", "median_flank_indel_rate")) else "–"`×
the flanks, the length changes of @sec-cdeii-steps. CDEII is constrained in length and
AT content, not in sequence, so it diverges as fast as unconstrained DNA, or faster.

**CDEI is invariant, CDEIII nearly so.** CDEI has π = 0 at
`r if (has_dv) sum(dv_per$element == "CDEI" & dv_per$pi == 0) else "–"` of 16 centromeres.
With 8 bp it cannot reach significance against the flanks (p =
`r if (has_dv) signif(pool("CDEI", "wilcoxon_p"), 2) else "–"`). CDEIII is invariant at
`r if (has_dv) sum(dv_per$element == "CDEIII" & dv_per$pi == 0) else "–"` centromeres but
carries single substitutions at others. Its median
(`r if (has_dv) signif(pool("CDEIII", "median_pi"), 2) else "–"`) is above the flank mean
(p = `r if (has_dv) signif(pool("CDEIII", "wilcoxon_p"), 2) else "–"`). The comparison is
against the flanks next to it, though, and those are not neutral either (next paragraph).
The protein-binding cores (CDEI CACRTG, CDEIII CCG) do not vary (@sec-kinetochore).

**Diversity rises towards the centromere.** Flank π is
`r if (has_dv) signif(dv_k$pi[dv_k$k == 1], 2) else "–"` in the 100 bp next to the CDEs,
`r if (has_dv) signif(dv_k$pi[dv_k$k == 2], 2) else "–"` one window out, and about
`r if (has_dv) signif(median(dv_k$pi[dv_k$k >= 10]), 1) else "–"` beyond 1 kb (medians over
32 flanks). It is mostly substitutions, and it is not one centromere: the innermost window
is above its own centromere's far-flank median in
`r if (has_dv) dv_k1_above else "–"` of 32 flanks. Bensasson 2008 found that yeast
centromeres themselves diverge fast. Here the excess also reaches a few hundred bp into
the flanks. Several explanations fit and cannot be separated here: recombination suppressed near the centromere, the AT-rich low-complexity sequence
next to it, and the transposon and tRNA landmarks of @sec-transposons. Against near-CEN
flanks, CDEII is still about
`r if (has_dv) round(pool("CDEII", "median_pi") / dv_k$pi[dv_k$k == 1], 1) else "–"`× higher.

Limits: 11 genomes, one sequence per assembly (collapsed heterozygotes included). π in
CDEI rests on 8 sites per centromere.
:::

---

## CDEII grammar and DNA shape {#sec-cdeii-grammar}

```{r gr-load}
gr <- load_grammar(params$data_dir)
has_gr <- !is.null(gr)
if (has_gr) {
  gr_pool <- filter(gr$grammar_null, centromere == "all")
  gp <- function(st, nl, col = "p", set_ = "modal")
    gr_pool[[col]][gr_pool$statistic == st & gr_pool$null == nl & gr_pool$set == set_]
  sh_pool <- filter(gr$shape_null, centromere == "all", set == "modal")
  sp <- function(st, nl, col = "p") sh_pool[[col]][sh_pool$statistic == st & sh_pool$null == nl]
  vs_all <- filter(gr$shape_variants_summary, centromere == "all")
  es_all <- filter(gr$shape_events_summary, centromere == "all")
  va <- function(f, col, set_ = "Helsen") vs_all[[col]][vs_all$feature == f & vs_all$set == set_]
  ea <- function(f, nl, col) es_all[[col]][es_all$feature == f & es_all$null == nl]
  n_single <- sum(gr$shape_variants$set == "Helsen" & gr$shape_variants$n_subs == 1)
  med_single <- gr$shape_variants |> filter(set == "Helsen", n_subs == 1) |>
    summarise(across(starts_with("pct_"), median))
}
fmt_p <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "–" else format(signif(x, 2), scientific = x < 1e-3)
```

@sec-diversity showed that CDEII changes fast in sequence but keeps its length and AT
content. Does it keep anything else? Two candidates come from the CDEII literature:
**A-tracts** (runs of A/T without a TpA step, which narrow the minor groove and bend
DNA) and their **phasing** about one helical turn apart, which could help CDEII wrap the
Cse4 nucleosome. Both are compared with two nulls of the same length and AT content.
Dinucleotide shuffles keep the dinucleotide composition and break any order. S288C
windows with AT within ±2 % (≥ 2 kb from a centromere) keep real-DNA structure, but at
CDEII's AT content of ~90 % they are rare. 200 of each per CDEII. The test set is the
population's modal allele per centromere (Helsen SD4, as in @sec-cdeii-steps); S288C gives
the same results (`grammar_null.tsv`).

An A-tract here is a run of ≥ 4 A/T with no TpA (`AAAATTTT` is one tract, `TTTTAAAA` two).
The phasing score is the fraction of tract-centre pairs up to 42 bp apart that sit within
±1 bp of a multiple of 10.5 bp. The second periodicity measure is the power of the AA/TT
dinucleotide signal at periods of 10–11 bp (1 = white noise).

```{r fig-grammar-null}
#| eval: !expr has_gr
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "A-tract statistics of the 16 modal CDEII alleles (black diamonds) against their nulls (coloured: median and 5–95 % of 200 sequences each). Hover for values and the per-centromere empirical p."
p_gr <- plot_grammar_null(gr)
save_fig(p_gr, "fig_f2_atract_phasing", 12, 5.5)
as_plotly(p_gr, 500)
```

```{r tbl-grammar}
#| eval: !expr has_gr
#| tbl-cap: "Across the 16 centromeres: median of (observed − null median), centromeres where the observed value is higher, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank p (16 pairs)."
gr_pool |> filter(set == "modal") |>
  transmute(Statistic = unname(GRAMMAR_LABELS[statistic]),
            Null = ifelse(null == "shuffle", "Dinucleotide shuffles", "AT-matched windows"),
            `Obs − null` = signif(obs, 2), Higher = paste0(n_higher, " / ", n_cen), p = signif(p, 2)) |>
  filter(!is.na(Statistic)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**Shape.** DNAshapeR (pentamer model) predicts minor-groove width (MGW), propeller twist
(ProT), roll and helix twist (HelT) along each CDEII. The two terminal bases or steps get
no value.

```{r fig-shape-profiles}
#| eval: !expr has_gr
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Predicted DNA shape along the 16 modal CDEII alleles (grey) and their median (black, where ≥ 8 alleles have the position). Alleles are 77–88 bp, so position aligns only the CDEI end."
p_sp <- plot_shape_profiles(gr)
save_fig(p_sp, "fig_f2_shape_profiles", 8, 7)
as_plotly(p_sp, 650)
```

```{r tbl-shape-null}
#| eval: !expr has_gr
#| tbl-cap: "Shape summaries of the 16 modal CDEII alleles against the nulls: median (observed − null median), centromeres higher, Wilcoxon p. Narrow: fraction of positions with MGW < 4 Å."
lab <- c(mean_mgw = "Mean MGW (Å)", frac_narrow = "Narrow-groove fraction", mean_prot = "Mean ProT (°)")
sh_pool |>
  transmute(Summary = lab[statistic], Null = ifelse(null == "shuffle", "Dinucleotide shuffles", "AT-matched windows"),
            `Obs − null` = signif(obs, 2), Higher = paste0(n_higher, " / ", n_cen), p = signif(p, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**Do natural variants keep the shape?** Helsen SD4 has
`r if (has_gr) va("MGW", "n") else "–"` CDEII alleles that differ from the modal allele by
1–10 substitutions and no indel. For each, the shape distance to the modal allele (mean
|Δ| over positions) is compared with 200 mutants that carry the same substitutions
(same b1 → b2) at random positions of the same base. The null is calibrated: a mutant
drawn from the null itself gets a uniform percentile (KS p ≥
`r if (has_gr) signif(min(vs_all$calib_ks_p[vs_all$set == "Helsen"]), 2) else "–"`).

Alleles share substitutions, though: a substitution carried by many alleles is counted
many times. The second test therefore uses each **unique substitution event** (centromere,
position, b1 → b2) once: `r if (has_gr) ea("MGW", "base", "n_events") else "–"` events. Its
shape change is ranked among all single mutants b1 → b2 at the other positions carrying
b1, exhaustively. The third test ranks it only among positions in the same trinucleotide
context (`r if (has_gr) ea("MGW", "trinuc", "n_events") else "–"` events with ≥ 5 such
positions). Mutation rates in yeast depend on the neighbouring bases. This last
comparison removes that.

```{r fig-shape-variants}
#| eval: !expr has_gr
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Where natural substitutions rank among null mutations by shape change (0 = the smallest change). With no preference the histograms are flat (dashed line). Top: Helsen alleles against spectrum-matched mutants. Middle and bottom: unique substitution events, against every same-base position and every same-trinucleotide position."
p_sv <- plot_shape_variants(gr)
save_fig(p_sv, "fig_f2_shape_variants", 11, 6)
as_plotly(p_sv, 560)
```

```{r tbl-shape-variants}
#| eval: !expr has_gr
#| tbl-cap: "Median percentile of natural shape change among null mutations (< 0.5 = smaller than random) and one-sided Wilcoxon p (percentile below 0.5)."
bind_rows(
  vs_all |> filter(set == "Helsen") |> transmute(Test = "Alleles, spectrum null", Feature = feature, n, median_pct, p_less),
  es_all |> transmute(Test = ifelse(null == "base", "Events, same base", "Events, same trinucleotide"),
                      Feature = feature, n = n_events, median_pct, p_less)) |>
  mutate(median_pct = signif(median_pct, 2), p_less = signif(p_less, 2)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Feature, values_from = c(median_pct, p_less), names_glue = "{Feature} {.value}") |>
  select(Test, n, starts_with("MGW"), starts_with("ProT"), starts_with("Roll"), starts_with("HelT")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
**CDEII is richer in A-tracts than AT-rich DNA, but its tracts are not phased.** Against
AT-matched genome windows, CDEII has more tracts at every centromere (median
+`r if (has_gr) signif(gp("n_tracts", "genomic", "obs"), 2) else "–"`, p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(gp("n_tracts", "genomic")) else "–"`). It also has more bases in
tracts, and stronger AA/TT power at 10–11 bp
(`r if (has_gr) gp("power", "genomic", "n_higher") else "–"`/16, p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(gp("power", "genomic")) else "–"`). Dinucleotide shuffles of CDEII
itself keep that power (p = `r if (has_gr) fmt_p(gp("power", "shuffle")) else "–"`).
The periodic AA/TT signal therefore comes from CDEII's dinucleotide make-up, not from how
the dinucleotides are ordered. The phasing score does not differ from either
null (p = `r if (has_gr) fmt_p(gp("phase", "shuffle")) else "–"` and
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(gp("phase", "genomic")) else "–"`): A-tracts do not sit one turn apart
more often than chance.

**Its order does one thing: it avoids long tracts.** Compared with its own shuffles,
CDEII has slightly more tracts and more bases in them, but a shorter longest tract
(median `r if (has_gr) signif(gp("max_tract", "shuffle", "obs"), 2) else "–"` bp, longer at
only `r if (has_gr) gp("max_tract", "shuffle", "n_higher") else "–"` of 16, p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(gp("max_tract", "shuffle")) else "–"`). The same A/T content is split
into many short tracts instead of a few long ones. The predicted shape follows: CDEII has a
narrower minor groove and more negative propeller twist than AT-matched genome windows at
every centromere. Against its own shuffles, only propeller twist stays lower
(`r if (has_gr) sp("mean_prot", "shuffle", "n_higher") else "–"`/16 higher, p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(sp("mean_prot", "shuffle")) else "–"`); MGW does not (p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(sp("mean_mgw", "shuffle")) else "–"`). Both are what the A-tract
arrangement predicts.

**Variants do not preserve shape beyond their mutational context.** At the allele level,
natural substitutions change shape less than the same substitutions placed elsewhere
(median percentile
`r if (has_gr) signif(va("Roll", "median_pct"), 2) else "–"`–`r if (has_gr) signif(va("ProT", "median_pct"), 2) else "–"`,
p down to `r if (has_gr) fmt_p(min(vs_all$p_less[vs_all$set == "Helsen"])) else "–"`). That
is mostly pseudo-replication. The `r if (has_gr) n_single else "–"` single-substitution
alleles alone give medians of
`r if (has_gr) paste(signif(range(unlist(med_single)), 2), collapse = "–") else "–"`. Counted once per unique event, a small preference remains for roll
(median `r if (has_gr) signif(ea("Roll", "base", "median_pct"), 2) else "–"`, p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(ea("Roll", "base", "p_less")) else "–"`) and MGW (p =
`r if (has_gr) fmt_p(ea("MGW", "base", "p_less")) else "–"`). Within the same trinucleotide
context it is gone (all medians
`r if (has_gr) paste(unique(signif(es_all$median_pct[es_all$null == "trinuc"], 2)), collapse = ", ") else "–"`,
p ≥ `r if (has_gr) fmt_p(min(es_all$p_less[es_all$null == "trinuc"])) else "–"`). That histogram is slightly U-shaped, with an excess at both ends. Some events change shape less than their context would predict and some change it more, and the two balance out.
Frequent events are no more shape-neutral than rare ones (Spearman ρ with assembly
count `r if (has_gr) signif(ea("Roll", "base", "rho_freq"), 1) else "–"`). Where
substitutions fall in CDEII is explained by their local sequence context. Predicted
shape adds no constraint that is visible here.

Limits: DNAshapeR is a pentamer model of free DNA, not of DNA on the Cse4 nucleosome or
under CBF3. Indel alleles (the length steps of @sec-cdeii-steps) are not tested; comparing
their phasing needs alignment-aware shape comparison. Helsen alleles share ancestry: the
allele test counts related strains as independent, and in the per-event test one event may
be a single mutation inherited by many strains or several independent ones.
:::

---

## Centromere tree vs genome tree {#sec-trees}

```{r tr-load}
tr <- load_trees(params$data_dir)
has_tr <- !is.null(tr)
if (has_tr) {
  tr_core <- filter(tr$core, is.na(strain))
  tr_cmp <- tr$compare
  tr_top <- tr$contrib |> group_by(strain) |> slice_max(contribution, n = 2, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    summarise(top = paste0(centromere, " (", signif(contribution, 2), ")", collapse = ", "))
  tr_disc <- tr$disc |> left_join(tr_top, by = "strain")
  tr_sw <- tr$swap
  tr_scan <- tr$scan
}
```

Do the 16 centromeres tell the same strain history as the genome? The **centromere tree**
uses the 16 per-centromere alignments of @sec-variants, concatenated
(`r if (has_tr) max(tr$blocks$end) else "–"` columns, 11 taxa). The **genome tree** uses the
minimap2 alignments of @sec-diversity, restricted to sites that each assembly covers with
exactly one alignment (no paralogous Ty, subtelomeric or collapsed duplicate sequence) and
that are not within 2 kb of a centromere, so the two trees share no sites.
That leaves `r if (has_tr) format(sum(tr_core$core), big.mark = ",") else "–"` sites
(`r if (has_tr) percent(sum(tr_core$core) / sum(tr_core$length), 0.1) else "–"` of the R64
nuclear genome), `r if (has_tr) format(sum(tr_core$variable), big.mark = ",") else "–"` of
them variable. Both matrices are K80 distances from the same code, and the trees are
neighbour-joining, midpoint-rooted (ape). Two comparisons follow. Robinson–Foulds counts
bipartitions present in one tree only. Mantel correlates the two distance matrices
(Spearman, 9,999 permutations).

```{r fig-tanglegram}
#| eval: !expr has_tr
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Genome tree (left) and centromere tree (right), neighbour-joining on K80 distances, midpoint-rooted; lines join the same strain."
plot_tanglegram(tr, "fig_h1_tanglegram")
```

```{r tbl-tree-compare}
#| eval: !expr has_tr
#| tbl-cap: "Tree comparison. nRF = RF / 2(n − 3)."
tr_cmp |> transmute(Taxa = n_taxa, RF = rf, `RF max` = rf_max, nRF = round(nrf, 2),
                    `Mantel r` = round(mantel_r, 3), `Mantel p` = mantel_p) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r tbl-discordance}
#| eval: !expr has_tr
#| tbl-cap: "Per strain: discordance = 1 − Spearman ρ between the strain's distances to the others in the centromere and genome matrices. Top centromeres: the two whose removal from the concatenation lowers the strain's discordance most (the drop in brackets)."
tr_disc |> transmute(Strain = strain, Discordance = round(discordance, 3), `Top centromeres` = top) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
**The centromeres follow the genome.** The two distance matrices correlate at Mantel
r = `r if (has_tr) round(tr_cmp$mantel_r, 2) else "–"` (p =
`r if (has_tr) tr_cmp$mantel_p else "–"`, the smallest possible with 9,999 permutations).
Pairs that are close in the genome are close at their centromeres. The trees share the
same clades: ADS + CFS, ANM + AVN, CCC + CFA, and BAH outside the rest. Yet
`r if (has_tr) tr_cmp$rf else "–"` of `r if (has_tr) tr_cmp$rf_max else "–"` bipartitions
differ (nRF `r if (has_tr) round(tr_cmp$nrf, 2) else "–"`). The deep, short internal branches
of the genome tree are not resolved by 1.9 kb of centromere. The most visible move is S288C,
which leaves its genome-tree position to join CCC + CFA. Per-strain discordance is highest for
`r if (has_tr) paste(head(tr_disc$strain, 2), collapse = " and ") else "–"`.

**Discordance at this size is not evidence of centromere-specific history.** We tested
whether the read-out can find a known event: one strain was given another strain's
sequence at the 4 centromeres where they differ most. The swapped strain should then
become the most discordant, with those 4 centromeres at the top of its list (spec check 8).
It passes on simulated data (tests). On the real alignment it mostly fails. For
`r if (has_tr) paste(tr_sw$strain, "←", tr_sw$donor) else "–"` (the most concordant strain,
the most distant donor), the most discordant strain becomes
`r if (has_tr) tr_sw$most_discordant else "–"` (the donor). The top 4 centromeres include
`r if (has_tr) length(intersect(strsplit(tr_sw$top_contributors, ",")[[1]], strsplit(tr_sw$swapped, ",")[[1]])) else "–"`
of the 4 swapped. Over all `r if (has_tr) nrow(tr_scan) else "–"` strain/donor pairs, the
swapped strain is the most discordant in
`r if (has_tr) percent(mean(tr_scan$most_discordant)) else "–"`. All 4 swapped centromeres
come out on top in `r if (has_tr) percent(mean(tr_scan$n_swapped_in_top == 4)) else "–"`
(median `r if (has_tr) median(tr_scan$n_swapped_in_top) else "–"` of 4). With this little power,
the discordances in the table, and the centromeres listed against them, are not read as
introgression or conversion at particular centromeres. More genomes, or reads to resolve
the collapsed assemblies, are needed before a per-centromere history can be called. Leave-one-out also dilutes
redundant signal: when several centromeres agree, dropping any one changes little.
:::

---

## Centromere length {#sec-length}

```{r fig-length-dist}
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of centromere length (CDEI start to CDEIII end) per centromere. Colour is the number of assemblies with that length. Hover for the assemblies in each cell."
dist_df <- length_distribution(aligned)
p_dist <- ggplot(dist_df, aes(centromere, sequence_length, fill = n, text = text)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = NULL, trans = "sqrt",
                       breaks = pretty_breaks(n = min(5, max(dist_df$n)))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks(n = 8), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Centromeres", y = "Centromere length, bp") +
  theme_cen() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right", legend.key.height = unit(1.6, "cm"),
        legend.key.width = unit(0.35, "cm"))
save_fig(p_dist, "fig02_length_distribution", 10, 6)
as_plotly(p_dist, 560)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
Each centromere has one dominant length — a single bright cell per column, at
`r min(aligned$sequence_length[aligned$delta_length == 0])`–`r max(aligned$sequence_length[aligned$delta_length == 0])`
bp where it matches S288C — with a few assemblies spread ±1–5 bp around it.
`r n_distinct(dist_df$centromere[dist_df$n > 0 & dist_df$sequence_length > 125])`
centromere has a length outside the usual window, the `r big$sequence_length` bp
CEN16 described below. Unlike the earlier 748-strain heat map, there is no tail of
short lengths: those were partial BLAST hits and cross-centromere matches, which the
pipeline now removes or repairs.
:::

```{r fig-length}
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: !expr if (length(unique(d$aligned$assembly)) > LARGE_SET) 12 else 1.6 + 0.42 * length(unique(d$aligned$assembly))
#| fig-cap: "Centromere length (CDEI start to CDEIII end) in every assembly. Colour is the difference from the S288C element of the same centromere; numbers are the length in bp. Hover for details."
len_df <- aligned |>
  mutate(text = paste0("<b>", assembly, "</b> · ", clade,
                       "<br>", centromere, ": ", sequence_length, " bp (S288C ", ref_length, ")",
                       "<br>CDEII ", cdeii_length, " bp · ", contig_name))
lim <- max(5, min(10, max(abs(len_df$delta_length))))
p_len <- ggplot(len_df, aes(centromere, assembly, fill = delta_length, text = text)) +
  geom_tile(colour = SURFACE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = DIV_LOW, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_HIGH, midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-lim, lim), oob = squish,
                       name = "Δ length vs S288C, bp") +
  guides(fill = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_cen() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"), legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"))
if (assembly_rows <= 30) {
  p_len <- p_len + geom_text(aes(label = sequence_length,
                                 colour = abs(delta_length) >= 0.7 * lim), size = 3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = INK, `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none")
}
if (large_set) {
  # raster without cell borders or numbers; one pixel row per assembly
  p_len <- ggplot(len_df, aes(centromere, assembly, fill = delta_length)) +
    geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = DIV_LOW, mid = DIV_MID, high = DIV_HIGH, midpoint = 0,
                         limits = c(-lim, lim), oob = squish,
                         name = "Δ length vs S288C, bp") +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste(assembly_rows, "assemblies")) +
    theme_cen() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"), legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"))
  save_fig(p_len, "fig03_length_vs_s288c", 11, 12)
  p_len
} else {
  save_fig(p_len, "fig03_length_vs_s288c", 11, 1.2 + 0.32 * assembly_rows)
  as_plotly(p_len, 150 + 42 * assembly_rows)
}
```

**How it was obtained.** Length is counted on the annotated locus (first base of
CDEI to last base of CDEIII), not on the BLAST alignment, whose ends stop wherever
the local alignment stops scoring.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
Most cells are within a few bp of S288C (median length
`r median(aligned$sequence_length)` bp; `r pct(mean(abs(aligned$delta_length) <= 2))`
of loci within ±2 bp). The columns that stand out are whole-centromere shifts shared
by most strains — CEN4 is longer than S288C in nearly every assembly, because S288C
carries a 7-bp deletion there (@sec-variants).

The extreme is **`r big$assembly` `r big$centromere`, `r big$sequence_length` bp
(+`r big$delta_length`)**: a `r big_ins$size`-bp insertion in CDEII
(`r big_ins$alt`), a tandem duplication of the adjacent sequence. BLAST reported it
as two overlapping pieces, and stitching them on their overlap would have collapsed
the duplicate and reported an ordinary 117 bp centromere; reading the locus from
the genome recovers it.
:::

---

## GC content {#sec-gc}

```{r fig-gc}
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "GC content per centromere as a raincloud: points are assemblies, the half-violin their density. Dashed line: median over all loci. Hover a point for the assembly."
rc <- raincloud_data(aligned, "GC")
rc$points <- rc$points |>
  mutate(text = paste0("<b>", assembly, "</b> · ", clade, "<br>", centromere,
                       ": GC ", percent(GC, 0.1), " (S288C ",
                       percent(gc_content(reference[as.character(centromere)]), 0.1), ")"))
gc_median <- median(aligned$GC)
p_gc <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = gc_median, linetype = "dashed", colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_polygon(data = rc$clouds, aes(x, y, group = centromere, fill = centromere,
                                     colour = centromere), alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = rc$points, aes(x, y, colour = centromere, text = text), size = 1.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = CEN_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = CEN_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(rc$cens), labels = rc$cens,
                     expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Centromeres", y = "GC content") +
  theme_cen() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), legend.position = "none",
        axis.line = element_line(colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.4),
        axis.ticks = element_line(colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.3))
save_fig(p_gc, "fig04_gc_raincloud", 11, 5.5)
as_plotly(p_gc, 540)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
Median GC is **`r percent(gc_median, 0.1)`** (S288C elements:
`r percent(median(gc_content(reference)), 0.1)`), against ~38 % genome-wide: the
element is dominated by the AT-rich CDEII. GC differs much more *between*
centromeres than *within* one — CEN13 sits near 20 %, CEN12 and CEN16 near 12 %, and
the strains of each centromere cluster around its own value. No centromere shows two
clusters; the CEN14 and CEN15 bimodality of the earlier 748-strain raincloud came
from cross-centromere hits. With `r n_asm` points per centromere the half-violins are
rough sketches of the density; they become informative as assemblies are added.
:::

---

## Sequence logos {#sec-logos}

**How they were obtained.** In each centromere's alignment a position frequency
matrix counts each base per column (gaps excluded). Each column is scored by its
**information content**

$$
I_i \;=\; 2 + \sum_{b \in \{A,C,G,T\}} p_{ib}\log_2 p_{ib} \quad \text{bits},
$$

and letters are drawn with height $p_{ib} \cdot I_i$: total stack height is
conservation, relative letter height is which base. With `r n_asm` sequences per
centromere most columns are fully conserved and stand at 2 bits; the informative
part is where they are not.

```{r fig-logos}
#| fig-cap: "Sequence logos of all 16 centromeres across the assemblies. Boxes: CDEI (left) and CDEIII (right), placed from the S288C element in each alignment; CDEII lies between them."
#| column: page
logo_df <- boxes |> mutate(seq_group = factor(as.character(centromere), CEN_LEVELS))
p_logo <- ggseqlogo(logo_matrices(aligned), method = "bits", ncol = 1)
# ggseqlogo facets in text order (CEN1, CEN10, ...); refacet in chromosome order
p_logo$data$seq_group <- factor(p_logo$data$seq_group, CEN_LEVELS)
for (i in seq_along(p_logo$layers)) {
  if (is.data.frame(p_logo$layers[[i]]$data) && "seq_group" %in% names(p_logo$layers[[i]]$data)) {
    p_logo$layers[[i]]$data$seq_group <- factor(p_logo$layers[[i]]$data$seq_group, CEN_LEVELS)
  }
}
p_logo <- suppressMessages(p_logo +
  facet_wrap(~seq_group, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  geom_rect(data = logo_df, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -0.05, ymax = 2.08),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.45) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 200, 10), expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 2))) +
  labs(x = "Alignment column", y = "Information content, bits") +
  theme_cen(10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(margin = margin(b = 1)),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "cm"))
save_fig(p_logo, "fig05_logos", 13, 17)
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig05_logos.png")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
CDEI and CDEIII stand at full height in every centromere; the dips are in between.
CDEII looks as it should — **stacks of A and T and almost nothing else**, with long
homopolymer runs — and its few full-height C and G letters are position-specific
signals worth noting. Column numbers are alignment coordinates and are not
comparable between centromeres.
:::

---

## Variants against S288C {#sec-variants}

```{r fig-variants}
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: !expr if (length(unique(d$aligned$assembly)) > LARGE_SET) 16 else 1.5 + 8 * (0.45 + 0.24 * length(unique(d$aligned$assembly)))
#| fig-cap: "Every difference from S288C. One row per assembly, one panel per centromere; shaded bands are CDEI and CDEIII. Hover for the position and the bases."
if (large_set) {
  # fraction of the centromere's assemblies with a variant of each type in each column
  n_cen <- aligned |> count(centromere, name = "n_cen")
  freq <- variants |> distinct(centromere, col, type, assembly) |>
    count(centromere, col, type) |> left_join(n_cen, by = "centromere") |>
    mutate(frac = n / n_cen)
  p_var <- ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = boxes, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = 1), fill = BAND) +
    geom_col(data = freq, aes(col, frac, fill = type), width = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = VARIANT_COLOURS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    facet_wrap(~centromere, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = "Alignment column", y = paste("Share of", assembly_rows, "assemblies")) +
    theme_cen(10) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
  save_fig(p_var, "fig06_variant_map", 13, 16)
  p_var
} else {
aln_len <- aligned |> distinct(centromere, ref_aligned_seq) |>
  transmute(centromere, len = nchar(ref_aligned_seq))
var_df <- variants |>
  mutate(text = paste0("<b>", assembly, "</b> · ", clade, "<br>", centromere, " ",
                       element, ", S288C position ", refpos, "<br>", type, ": ",
                       ref, " → ", alt))
rows_df <- expand_grid(aln_len, assembly = levels(aligned$assembly)) |>
  mutate(assembly = factor(assembly, levels(aligned$assembly)))
p_var <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = boxes, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0.5, ymax = assembly_rows + 0.5),
            fill = BAND) +
  geom_segment(data = rows_df, aes(x = 1, xend = len, y = assembly, yend = assembly),
               colour = AXIS, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_tile(data = var_df, aes(col, assembly, fill = type, text = text),
            width = 0.9, height = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = VARIANT_COLOURS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~centromere, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Alignment column", y = NULL) +
  theme_cen(10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
save_fig(p_var, "fig06_variant_map", 13, 2 + 8 * (0.35 + 0.16 * assembly_rows))
as_plotly(p_var, 260 + 8 * (70 + 24 * assembly_rows)) |> layout(margin = list(b = 80))
}
```

**How it was obtained.** In each alignment, every column is compared with the S288C
row: a base against a different base is a **substitution**, a base against a gap in
S288C an **insertion**, a gap against an S288C base a **deletion**. Consecutive
indel columns are one event.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
The map is mostly empty inside the bands and busy between them. Two kinds of
pattern are worth telling apart:

- **Columns where most strains differ** — the same variant in nearly every row.
  These are places where **S288C carries the unusual allele**: CEN4's 7-bp
  `TTTTAAT` insertion relative to S288C (S288C's CEN4 is its shortest, 111 bp),
  and a handful of CDEIII positions in CEN3, CEN6 and CEN10.
- **Variants in one or a few rows** — private or clade-level changes, which is
  where strain-to-strain diversity actually shows.

The two Wine/European assemblies (ADS, CFS) carry the fewest differences, consistent
with S288C's largely European ancestry.
:::

```{r tbl-shared}
#| tbl-cap: "Variants carried by at least 80 % of the assemblies: positions where S288C, not the strains, is the exception."
events |>
  group_by(centromere, element, refpos, type, ref, alt) |>
  summarise(n = n_distinct(sample), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 0.8 * n_asm) |>
  arrange(centromere, refpos) |>
  transmute(Centromere = centromere, Element = element, `S288C position` = refpos,
            Type = type,
            `S288C` = if_else(type == "Insertion", "(none)", ref),
            Strains = if_else(type == "Deletion", "(none)", alt),
            `Assemblies` = paste0(n, "/", n_asm)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

---

## Where variation sits: CDEI, CDEII, CDEIII {#sec-elements}

```{r fig-elements}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Variants per kb of element, per centromere (points) and overall (black bar). Rates are per assembly-base: count ÷ (assemblies × element length in S288C)."
el_df <- rates |>
  mutate(text = paste0("<b>", centromere, " ", element, "</b><br>", n, " ",
                       tolower(kind), " in ", n_assemblies, " assemblies<br>",
                       fmt(per_kb), " per kb"))
el_mean <- rate_mean |> mutate(text = paste0("<b>All centromeres, ", element, "</b><br>",
                                             fmt(per_kb), " ", tolower(kind), " per kb"))
p_el <- ggplot(el_df, aes(element, per_kb)) +
  geom_point(aes(text = text), colour = SERIES1, alpha = 0.6, size = 2,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 2)) +
  geom_errorbar(data = el_mean, aes(element, ymin = per_kb, ymax = per_kb, text = text),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.45, linewidth = 0.8, colour = INK) +
  facet_wrap(~kind, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Per kb of element") +
  theme_cen()
save_fig(p_el, "fig07_element_rates", 9, 4)
as_plotly(p_el, 430)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
This is the comparison the analysis was built for, and it comes out as expected.
Substitutions run at **`r fmt(rate_of("CDEII", "Substitutions"))` per kb in
CDEII**, against `r fmt(rate_of("CDEIII", "Substitutions"))` in CDEIII and
`r fmt(rate_of("CDEI", "Substitutions"))` in CDEI. **`r n_indel_cdeii` of
`r n_indel` indel events fall in CDEII** — the protein-binding elements tolerate
substitutions only, and few of those.

Two cautions. The CDEIII rate is inflated by the positions where S288C is the odd
one out (@tbl-shared): a single S288C-private base shows up as a variant in nearly
every strain. And CDEI is 8 bp, so its rate rests on a handful of events.
:::

---

## Substitution spectrum {#sec-spectrum}

```{r fig-spectrum}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Substitutions from the S288C base to the strain's base. Top: counts. Bottom: the same counts divided by the number of assembly-sites where S288C has that base (per kb)."
sp <- spectrum$total |>
  mutate(text_n = paste0("<b>", class, "</b><br>", n, " substitutions"),
         text_r = paste0("<b>", class, "</b><br>", fmt(per_kb), " per kb of S288C ",
                         ref, " sites (", n, " / ", comma(sites), ")"))
sp_long <- bind_rows(
  sp |> transmute(class, value = n, text = text_n, measure = "Substitutions"),
  sp |> transmute(class, value = per_kb, text = text_r, measure = "Per kb of sites")
) |> mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("Substitutions", "Per kb of sites")))
p_sp <- ggplot(sp_long, aes(class, value, text = text)) +
  geom_col(fill = SERIES1, width = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "S288C base \u2192 strain base", y = NULL) + theme_cen()
save_fig(p_sp, "fig08_substitution_spectrum", 9, 6.5)
as_plotly(p_sp, 600)
```

```{r fig-spectrum-cen}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Substitution counts by centromere and class."
sp_cen <- spectrum$by_cen |>
  filter(centromere %in% aligned$centromere) |>
  mutate(text = paste0("<b>", centromere, " ", class, "</b><br>", n, " substitutions"))
p_sp_cen <- ggplot(sp_cen, aes(class, centromere, fill = n, text = text)) +
  geom_tile(colour = SURFACE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = SEQ_LOW, high = SEQ_HIGH, name = "Substitutions",
                      guide = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top")) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  geom_tile(data = filter(sp_cen, n == 0), fill = BAND, colour = SURFACE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "S288C base → strain base", y = NULL) +
  theme_cen() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"), legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"))
save_fig(p_sp_cen, "fig09_substitutions_by_centromere", 8, 6)
as_plotly(p_sp_cen, 600)
```

**How it was obtained.** Every substitution is classed by S288C base → strain base.
The bottom panel divides each class by its **opportunity**: the number of
assembly-sites where S288C has that base and the strain has any base.

```{r spectrum-numbers}
at <- sp |> filter(class %in% c("A→T", "T→A"))
top_rate <- sp |> slice_max(per_kb, n = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading it
In raw counts **A→T and T→A lead** (`r pct(sum(at$n) / sum(sp$n))` of all
substitutions), the shape the earlier 748-strain figure showed. But A and T are
also most of what there is to substitute. **Per available site the order changes:**
the highest rates are `r paste0(top_rate$class, " (", fmt(top_rate$per_kb), ")", collapse = ", ")`
per kb. The A↔T excess is mostly composition — abundant, not elevated — and the
rare G and C positions of the centromere change at the higher per-site rate, led
by the transition G→A.

With `r n_asm` assemblies the per-site rates of C- and G-initiated classes rest on
tens of events; they are the numbers most likely to move as more genomes are added.
:::

---

## Split hits and duplicated loci {#sec-splits}

```{r tbl-splits}
#| tbl-cap: "Loci that BLAST reported in more than one piece."
splits <- aligned |> filter(blast_pieces > 1)
if (nrow(splits) == 0) {
  knitr::kable(tibble(Note = "None."))
} else {
  splits |> transmute(Assembly = assembly, Centromere = centromere,
                      `BLAST pieces` = blast_pieces,
                      `Stitched BLAST length, bp` = blast_length,
                      `Annotated length, bp` = sequence_length,
                      `S288C length, bp` = ref_length) |>
    knitr::kable()
}
```

In a complete assembly a split hit is usually a structural change inside the
centromere — here, the tandem duplication described in @sec-length — rather than a
fragmented contig.

---

## What these figures do and do not establish {#sec-caveats}

**Supported by these data:**

- The pipeline finds exactly one locus per centromere in every assembly, on the
  expected chromosome, including rearranged ones, with CDEI and CDEIII placed at
  their motifs.
- Variation concentrates in CDEII, both as substitutions and as all of the indels;
  CDEI and CDEIII carry few substitutions and no indels.
- The raw A↔T dominance of the spectrum is largely compositional.

::: {.callout-caution}
## Limits to keep in view

1. **`r n_asm` assemblies.** Enough to validate the method and see the shape of each
   statistic; not enough for population frequencies or for comparing clades.
2. **Variants are differences from S288C, not mutations.** Without an outgroup
   (*S. paradoxus*) the direction of change cannot be polarised, and @tbl-shared
   shows S288C is itself the unusual allele at several positions.
3. **Counts are per assembly, not per event.** Related strains share variants by
   descent; nothing here corrects for the phylogeny.
4. **Collapsed assemblies show one allele per centromere.**
   `r sum(grepl("_collapsed", strains$assembly))` of `r n_asm` assemblies are
   heterozygous genomes merged into one sequence; any heterozygosity at a centromere
   is invisible in them.
5. **The alignment is still the weak link.** MAFFT on 90 % AT sequence can shift
   homopolymer runs; a shifted run turns one indel into a few apparent
   substitutions. Lengths (@sec-length) do not depend on the alignment; the variant
   map and spectrum do.
:::

**Next steps:** run the remaining ScRAP assemblies; add *S. paradoxus* to polarise
the variants; join per-strain CDEII length and variant load to clade, ecology and
the `Phenotypes_8391Traits/` growth traits.
